title: A second refund claim journals a second RefundClaimedEvent: the aggregate records no claim, so it cannot refuse one
description:
Found 2026-09-19 by the lane that built the refund-claim flow (libspiffy-cqc part b, V-99), and confirmed on main.

PaymentChannelAggregate._handleClaimRefund now guards three things: the channel is past its lockTime, the caller is the client, and the channel is not already 'closed' or 'rejected' (that last guard is new in V-99). What it does NOT guard is a claim on a channel that has already been claimed.

The reason is structural, not an oversight: _applyRefundClaimed sets status to 'expired', and 'expired' MUST stay claimable - expire-then-claim is the required convergence path, because an expiry observed first records the refund without broadcasting it (V-86) and the claim is what carries the broadcast. So status alone cannot distinguish 'expired, never claimed' from 'expired by a claim'. Nothing in ChannelState records that a claim happened, so the aggregate has nothing to test.

Effect today: a repeated public ClaimChannelRefundCommand re-broadcasts the same transaction (harmless - same txid, and BSV is first-seen-wins) and journals a SECOND RefundClaimedEvent. State converges: _applyRefundClaimed is idempotent, the projection's _firstClosingTxId keeps the first txid, and _recordReturnLegInWallet no-ops on a transaction the wallet holds. So this is a duplicate ending in the journal, not corruption.

It is worth closing anyway, for the case the convergence does not cover: the second claim may carry a DIFFERENT refundTxHex, because ClaimRefundCommand.refundTxHex is caller-supplied. Then the journal asserts the channel ended twice with two different transactions, only one of which can be true. The projection already handles the conflict honestly (V-81: a conflicting second txid is logged, never allowed to replace the first), so the read model stays right - but the journal is the permanent record and it should not say something that cannot be true.

Fix shape: a refundClaimedTxId (nullable) on ChannelState, set by _applyRefundClaimed, and a guard refusing a claim when it is already set - or accepting one only when it names the same txid, which keeps a retried claim idempotent. Remember a channel state change needs FOUR places: ChannelState, copyWith, the snapshot toMap/fromMap, and FullChannelStateResponse.

Test: claim twice, assert exactly one RefundClaimedEvent in the journal; claim twice with two different refund transactions, assert the second is refused and names why.
close_reason: Fixed as V-109 (payment-channel seam, pass 1). ubl0: the client and server halves now share one _checkPaymentInvariants; the two balance-mismatch messages became one naming both sides. 07mx: ChannelState.refundClaimedTxId added in all four places, a repeat of the same claim is answered without journaling, a claim naming a different transaction is refused.

title: Plugin funding contract cannot express a non-P2PKH input, so plugin payments take P2PKH funding only
description:
Found 2026-09-18 by the libspiffy-8egy lane (V-83); this is what paths B and C of that bead need.

PluginTransactionRequest hands a TransactionBuilderPlugin the funding UTXOs and one SVPublicKey each; the plugin then calls spendFromOutpointWithSigner(request.signer, outpoint, seq, P2PKHUnlockBuilder(publicKeys[i])), and typically rebuilds the locking script as P2PKH from utxo.address rather than using utxo.scriptPubKey (see the in-repo fake at test/integration/coordinator_aggregate_signing_test.dart:970-980). The plugin owns the unlocking script, so libspiffy cannot make a plugin-built transaction spend a bare multisig or P2PK wallet output. ProvisionFundingMessage and plugin payments therefore still exclude those outputs (guard retained deliberately in payment_coordinator_actor.dart: handing them over would produce an invalid transaction instead of a clear refusal).

Scope:
- Extend PluginTransactionRequest with per-funding-UTXO unlocking-script builder FACTORIES. Factories, not instances: buildWithSigner re-runs build across passes, and a shared instance would accumulate signatures.
- Add an opt-in on TransactionBuilderPlugin so plugins that do not implement it keep receiving P2PKH-only funding (no silent breakage of existing plugins).
- Carry the real locking script (utxo.scriptPubKey) rather than letting the plugin reconstruct it from the address.
- Give _AggregateBackedSigner a per-signature cache key: it currently caches by 'sighashType:digest', so a second signer.sign() on the same input returns the SAME signature, which cannot satisfy an m-of-n input for m >= 2. (aggregate_signing_client._ownerOf already resolves owners for multisig and P2PK subscripts - that part needs nothing.)

Test: a plugin payment funded by a bare-multisig and a P2PK wallet UTXO, each input verified with dartsv.Interpreter().correctlySpends against its own locking script.

title: BenfordCoordinatorActor blocks its own mailbox for the whole split run, so broadcast outcomes cannot be processed
description:
Found while making the UTXO-splitting seam production-ready (V-108).

_handleSplitCommand awaits _splitSingleUtxo for EVERY source UTXO sequentially, inside onMessage. Each source costs up to: reserve (10 s timeout) + generate targetUtxoCount addresses (30 s) + sign (20 s) + record (30 s). maxUtxosToSplit defaults to null, which means ALL available UTXOs, so a wallet with 50 UTXOs can hold the coordinator's mailbox for a very long time.

Two consequences:
(1) No other split command is served meanwhile.
(2) _SplitBroadcastOutcome messages queue BEHIND the loop. _awaitBroadcast runs outside the mailbox and tells the outcome back in, but that message cannot be handled until the loop finishes, so _replyIfSettled cannot run and the earlier broadcasts' answers pile up. The reply is correct in the end, but the actor is doing the one thing the audit calls out as a defect class ('actor handlers that block their own mailbox', section 1).

This is the same shape as the fix already applied to the broadcast half: run the per-source work outside the mailbox and hand results back through it. The pending-reply bookkeeping (_PendingSplitReply, allStarted, awaiting) is already built for that.

Test: send a split for N sources with a wallet that is slow to record, and assert that a second message sent to the coordinator is handled before the loop ends (or that a broadcast outcome for source 1 is processed while source 2 is still being built).
notes: Commit 5b55c78 (V-108) refers to this bead as 'libspiffy-mgm2', which is not an id that exists. This is the bead it meant. The audit row for V-108 names it correctly.

title: Postgres storeWallet REPLACES metadata_json while Isar and in-memory merge: documented contract violated, metadata silently lost
description:
Split out of libspiffy-el95 (item 7) by the 19 Sep triage, and verified directly. This is NOT the doc bug the bead called it - it is a cross-backend contract violation that loses user data on one backend.

THE CONTRACT, stated twice:
read_model_storage.dart:42-45 - 'Creates the wallet when no metadata row exists (including after deleteWallet); otherwise MERGES into the existing row.'
read_model_storage.dart:24-25 - 'Rules every backend follows (audit 2026-09-14 S-15, S-19)'.
And AGENTS.md: 'If three storage backends implement the same interface, they handle the same edge cases.'

THE THREE BACKENDS (all verified by reading them):
- Isar (isar_wallet_storage.dart:135-138): MERGES - existingMeta.addAll(metadata)
- In-memory (in_memory_wallet_storage.dart:173-179): MERGES - {...?existing, ...?metadata}
- Postgres (postgres_wallet_storage.dart:107): REPLACES - metadata_json = COALESCE(@metadataJson, wallet_metadata.metadata_json)

COALESCE only preserves the old document when the WHOLE incoming map is null. Any non-null metadata map overwrites the entire JSON document, dropping every key the caller did not resupply. The two neighbouring columns (:105-106) use COALESCE correctly because they are scalars; the bug is that a JSON DOCUMENT was treated as one.

AND THE IN-MEMORY BACKEND'S OWN COMMENT ASSERTS THE FALSE STATE OF AFFAIRS: 'Merge with the existing record (as the Isar and Postgres backends do)'. Postgres does not.

PROOF THE DIVERGENCE IS REAL AND UNTESTED: two tests run the IDENTICAL scenario.
- wallet_storage_test.dart:115-142 (in-memory): stores {'version': 1}, then {'confirmedBalance': '100'}, and asserts the merged {'version': 1, 'confirmedBalance': '100'}.
- postgres_integration_test.dart:685-704: the SAME two calls with the SAME values - but the metadata assertion is ABSENT. It asserts only the network. On Postgres that sequence yields {'confirmedBalance': '100'} and version:1 is gone.

BLAST RADIUS: partially masked because three of four lib/ callers read-modify-write in Dart first (wallet_projection.dart:270-282, :392-402, :1131-1145 all spread the existing map). The exposed paths are (a) wallet_projection._handleWalletCreated (:228-245), which writes a FRESH map with no spread - on replay this wipes host entries and derived keys on Postgres, and _recalculateAndPersistForWallet restores only some balances, not host metadata; and (b) any host calling the public storeWallet directly, which the documented contract tells them is safe with a partial map.

WHY IT SURVIVED: storeWallet IS covered by contract tests - wallet_lifecycle_contract.dart and wallet_metadata_types_contract.dart both run on all three backends - but neither covers merge semantics. The merge rule is the one storeWallet rule left duplicated per-backend instead of shared. That is exactly why it diverged.

FIX: the SQL is one expression (metadata_json = wallet_metadata.metadata_json || @metadataJson, or a jsonb merge). The WORK is moving the merge rule into a shared contract test and collapsing the two divergent per-backend duplicates above. The fail-first test MUST be a contract test in test/storage/, not a fourth copy - it will fail on Postgres only, which is the proof.

Check whether the column is json or jsonb: || merge needs jsonb. If it is json, a small migration or a cast is needed (next free migration is v025). No Isar regeneration.

Also fix the false in-memory comment.
close_reason: Fixed as V-106: Postgres storeWallet now merges metadata_json (JSONB ||, no migration) as the documented contract and the other two backends do; getWallet's metadata is always a map; the merge rule moved into the shared wallet lifecycle contract test and the two divergent per-backend duplicates collapsed into it; the false in-memory comment corrected and the no-removal rule documented.

title: Sweep: commands and events the aggregates can handle that nothing in lib/ ever sends
description:
Filed 2026-09-18 after the same defect turned up three times in three different beads. This is the systematic version of what was found by accident.

THE PATTERN: an aggregate handles a command, the command has tests, and nothing in lib/ ever constructs it. The capability looks present and is not reachable, so a whole branch of the protocol is dead while reading as finished.

Confirmed instances so far:
- FinalizeCloseCommand - constructed nowhere until V-86 (libspiffy-f5p2). A cooperatively closed channel therefore hung in `closing` FOREVER, and ChannelClosedEvent was unreachable, including channel_p2p_adapter._onChannelClosed which sends the peer channel_closed. Nobody noticed because no test drove a full close to completion.
- ClaimRefundCommand - still constructed only in tests (libspiffy-cqc part b). The refund claim flow does not exist.
- UpdateUTXOConfirmationsCommand - reachable only from internals.dart, nothing in lib/ sends it; deprecated in V-78 rather than kept alive.

A RELATED PATTERN, same root: a placeholder that reads as done. V-86 found fullySignedPaymentTxHex: "" with the comment "Would need to combine sigs - simplified for now", which meant NO side ever held a settlement transaction and its txid was unknowable. The comment was six words in a 2000-line file.

SCOPE:
1. Enumerate every command and event type the aggregates handle (wallet, channel, invoice, deferred payment) and, for each, find the construction sites in lib/ (excluding tests). Report every type with zero lib/ senders.
2. For each, decide: wire it up (it is a real gap, like FinalizeCloseCommand was), deprecate it (nothing correct left for it to do, like UpdateUTXOConfirmationsCommand), or record why it is legitimately caller-only public API.
3. Grep for placeholder comments that mark unfinished behaviour - "simplified for now", "would need", "TODO", "for now", "not implemented", "placeholder" - in lib/ only, and triage each: real gap, or a note that outlived its code.
4. Check the reverse direction too: events an aggregate emits that no projection handles, so the fact is journaled and never reaches a read model. (RefundClaimedEvent.refundTxId was exactly this until V-81.)

Report the inventory even for the ones needing no action - the value is the list, so the next reader does not have to rediscover it.

This is a survey first, not a fix-everything task. Expect it to produce several beads.
close_reason: Survey delivered: doc/reachability-sweep-2026-09-18.md, plus V-87/88/89 and beads vspy, soui, wm8g, iftu

title: Channels: no public command to retry funding, or to re-send channel_open for an open channel whose message was lost
description: From libspiffy-fsy/36f (lane C). Restart recovery covers in-flight opens, but a host cannot explicitly retry a failed funding broadcast or re-send channel_open when the peer never received it.
close_reason:
Fixed as V-100 (commit 60a2353). Two public commands, each with a public outcome event: RetryChannelFundingCommand(channelId) -> ChannelFundingRetriedEvent re-broadcasts a client channel's funding transaction after a failed broadcast, and ResendChannelOpenCommand(channelId) -> ChannelOpenResentEvent sends channel_open again, rebuilt from journaled state, journaling nothing.

Two commands rather than one with a mode: the preconditions are mutually exclusive (refundSigned vs open), one broadcasts a transaction and changes the journal while the other sends a single message and changes nothing, and each refusal names the other command so a host that picks wrong is told which one it wanted.

The retry takes ONLY a channel id and reads the funding transaction from FullChannelStateResponse. That is the point: the gap was already written down by hand in two end-to-end tests, which retried by reaching past the public API (channelManager.tell(OpenChannelMessage(...))) and reading fundingTxId out of a storage row because no public command carried it. Both now drive the new command with their assertions intact.

Retrying was already safe at the aggregate - StartFundingBroadcastCommand deliberately permits a second start, double-recording is guarded three ways, and inputs are left deferSpend-reserved until ARC accepts, so a retry can only re-broadcast the same transaction. The seam was all that was missing.

THE LARGER FINDING, which the bead did not anticipate: the naive repair actively harms the channel. channel_open is emitted from exactly one place, edge-triggered on ChannelOpenedEvent; nothing reads state and re-emits. So re-driving the open flow for an already-open channel hits the aggregate's status != refundSigned guard, returns a failed ChannelOpenedResponse, and routes to _reportFailure(tellPeer: true) - sending channel_error to the counterparty. A host repairing a lost message would instead have told the peer the channel was abandoned. Neither new command can reach that path. Relatedly the server's inbound handler now treats a channel_open repeating the SAME funding output as a no-op answered success, because otherwise the peer answers the repair with the very message that says the channel failed; a repeat naming a different output is still refused.

Tests: test/actors/payment_channel_repair_test.dart (10), a new group in channel_p2p_adapter_test.dart (6), a new group in channel_open_coordinator_e2e_test.dart (4). Mutations verified on main include the idempotence guard disabled ('Bob answered a repeated channel_open with channel_error' - the harm itself), the resend precondition, the funding txid not read from state, and the coordinator dispatch arms deleted (six e2e tests red).

Still open and NOT covered by this: there is no startup sweep of channels stuck in refundSigned or fundingBroadcastInFlight. Recovery remains reactive and these commands are the host's manual lever over it. Also untouched: libspiffy-z5uo (inputs reserved forever after a funding failure).

title: No startup sweep of channels stuck in refundSigned or fundingBroadcastInFlight; recovery is reactive only
description:
Found 2026-09-19 by the libspiffy-1n3 survey, and left open by V-100.

Restart recovery (libspiffy-36f) is purely REACTIVE. ChannelP2PAdapter's _sequenced/_restore/_adopt fire only when an inbound stimulus carrying a channelId arrives - a peer message in the readsRecord set, a channel event, or a manager response. Nothing sweeps persisted channels at startup.

So a channel left in refundSigned with fundingBroadcastInFlight, or one whose funding broadcast failed, sits there until something external pokes it. If the counterparty has gone silent - which is the exact circumstance in which the funding failed or the channel_open was lost - nothing ever will.

V-100 gave the HOST a manual lever over this: RetryChannelFundingCommand and ResendChannelOpenCommand. That is deliberate and consistent with 'the library records, the app decides' - the app knows whether it still wants the channel. But it means an app that does not poll its own channel list will never notice one is stuck, because the library surfaces nothing.

The question this bead is for: should the library, at startup, ENUMERATE channels in a non-terminal state and tell the app about them (an event, or a queryable list), without acting on them? Recording the observation is the library's job; deciding to retry is the app's. That split would keep V-100's commands as the only actors while removing the need for the app to know to look.

Do NOT make this an automatic retry sweep. A funding broadcast whose outcome was lost may have reached the mempool, and BSV is first-seen-wins; re-driving channels on startup without the app asking is the library deciding policy.

Related: libspiffy-z5uo (nothing ever releases the inputs a failed funding reserved) is the other half of what an app needs to resolve a stuck channel - retry it, or abandon it and get the money back.

Test: persist channels in refundSigned, fundingBroadcastInFlight and open; restart; assert the app is told about the first two and not the third, and that nothing was retried or journaled by the sweep itself.
close_reason: Fixed as V-112. The coordinator sweeps the read model once at startup, off its mailbox, and emits UnfinishedChannelsFoundEvent per wallet with channels that started opening and never reached open (channel id, state, funding amount, lock time, counterparty peer id). It reports and does nothing else - no retry, no journal, no peer message - because a funding broadcast whose outcome was lost may already be in a mempool and BSV is first-seen-wins. Nothing is emitted when nothing is stuck; a read model that throws is logged and swallowed.

title: ReadModelStorage has no single-outpoint UTXO lookup, so every UTXO event loads the wallet's whole spend history
description:
Split out of libspiffy-3gd (item 5) by the 19 Sep triage. Premise confirmed, and the code says so out loud.

wallet_projection.dart:515-523 carries the acknowledgement:
  /// ...ReadModelStorage has no single-outpoint lookup, so
  /// one full load per event remains.
  Future<_UtxoRows> _loadUtxoRows(String walletId) async =>
      _UtxoRows(await _storage.getUTXOs(walletId, includeSpent: true));

_loadUtxoRows has THIRTEEN call sites - one per UTXO event handler (wallet_projection.dart:465, 621, 640, 691, 701, 732, 760, 784, 850, 930, 995, 1685). Each loads every UTXO the wallet has ever had, INCLUDING SPENT ones, and most then do a single rows.find(txid, vout). The cost grows without bound with spend history, and a wallet's spend history is never purged (by design - data retention).

The read side is the only gap: deleteUTXO(walletId, txid, vout) is already outpoint-addressed (read_model_storage.dart:202). The read surface is getUTXOs / getAvailableUTXOs / getPaymentUTXOs / getUTXOsByPlugin / upsertUTXO.

- single outpoint: the ~13 projection handlers, though several also need the full set for _recalculateAndPersistForWallet, so the win is partial for those

No migration needed: the Postgres primary key and the Isar utxoKey composite index already exist.

Per the protocol a performance fix must be OBSERVED by the test - rows read, the index used, query count - never wall-clock. Isar has a rows-read harness for exactly this: IsarWalletStorage.onQuery (isar_wallet_storage.dart:54-72) and test/storage/isar_query_access_test.dart, whose _Trace.rowsInRange counts what Isar actually reads.

- getUTXOsByTxid(walletId, txid, {includeSpent}) - one transaction's outputs.

The S-16 scoping test caught that the moment the new method was added to it.

title: A cancelled, failed or reclaimed payment's own change output stays pending forever
description:
Found by the libspiffy-87a lane; verified separately in lib/src/core/wallet/deferred_payments.dart.

When a deferred payment is recorded, its own outputs (the change back to us) are created as pending UTXOs; only a confirmation promotes them (the V-56 rule: confirming a transaction makes its own pending outputs available). DeferredPayments._applyResolution, which handles both DeferredTransactionFailedEvent and DeferredTransactionCancelledEvent (and now the reclaim path), walks ONLY the released inputs. Nothing touches the transaction's own outputs. A payment that is cancelled, failed or reclaimed can never be confirmed, so its change output sits at pending forever, from a transaction that can never be mined.

Cosmetic today: pending UTXOs are excluded from spendable balance, so no funds are misreported. But the rows accumulate without bound for any wallet that cancels or reclaims regularly, and they are visible in UTXO listings as funds that look like they are on the way.

RETENTION: do NOT delete the UTXO rows. Per spv-understanding.md nothing is deleted or overwritten. The fix is a status that says what is true - the output belongs to a transaction that will never be mined - not a purge. Decide what that status is (a new terminal one, or reuse of an existing one) and say why.

Test: record a deferred payment with change, cancel it, assert the change output is not left pending indefinitely and is not counted as incoming.

title: Isar getMerkleProofsByStatusChangedSince has no (status, statusChangedAt) index and violates the stated read-model contract
description:
Split out of libspiffy-el95 (item 1) by the 19 Sep triage. Premise confirmed, and the 'is this testable' question has a YES answer.

libspiffy_schemas.dart:192-193 gives MerkleProofEntity.status exactly one composite:
  @Index(composite: [CompositeIndex('blockHeight')])
statusChangedAt (line 196) has NO @Index at all. The query at isar_wallet_storage.dart:1101-1106 filters within the status prefix:
  .where().statusEqualToAnyBlockHeight(status.name).filter().statusChangedAtGreaterThan(since, include: true)
Its own doc-comment already admits it uses 'the status prefix of the (status, blockHeight) index'. So Isar reads EVERY rejected/orphaned proof ever stored and discards most in the filter.

ISAR IS THE ODD BACKEND OUT. Postgres already has the right index: migration v018_merkle_proof_status_changed_index.dart creates idx_merkle_proofs_status_changed ON merkle_proofs (status, status_changed_at). And ReadModelStorage states the contract for ALL backends at read_model_storage.dart:620-621: 'Backends read only those rows (a (status, status changed at) index).' Isar does not honour that sentence. So this is a cross-backend contract violation, not merely a missing optimisation.

TESTABILITY - the important part. Isar 3 has no query explain (isar_wallet_storage.dart:58-59 says so). But this repo built its own substitute and it is the STANDING standard for exactly this: IsarWalletStorage.onQuery (isar_wallet_storage.dart:54-72, _traced wraps every query) plus test/storage/isar_query_access_test.dart, whose _Trace.rowsInRange replays the where clauses and counts the rows Isar actually reads. getMerkleProofsByStatusChangedSince is NOT currently in that file - only the getMerkleProofsByStatus height variants are (:528, :560). Precedent to copy is :560, 'hg0: orphaned proofs ... read from the (status, blockHeight) index'.

So a fail-first rows-read test is fully doable under the no-wall-clock rule: assert rowsInRange equals the few rows changed since, not the whole rejected corpus.

Regeneration: YES - @Index compiles into libspiffy_schemas.g.dart with index ids baked in, so build_runner must re-run. Isar 3 auto-migrates indexes on open and this project has no schema version bump. Two @Index annotations on one property is already done here (libspiffy_schemas.dart:371-373 on DeferredPaymentEntity.walletId), so the shape is established. Add a migration test too: isar_index_migration_test.dart:200-237 (the hg0 test) is the exact template for proving an old store still answers.

title: A receive replayed after a restart credits the wallet but emits no CoordinatorEvent (SPVActor has no coordinator reference)
description: From libspiffy-vfai (V-63). A parked receive replayed in a new process credits the UTXO, but the app sees no TransactionImportedEvent on the public stream: the original reply target was an ActorRef that died with the previous process, and SPVActor holds no coordinator reference to emit on. An app restarted between the park and the header therefore learns of the funds only by polling the read model. Decide how a replayed receive reaches the public stream (a coordinator reference on SPVActor, or the projection emitting for replayed receives) and implement it. Test: park a receive, restart, deliver the header, assert a coordinator event is emitted as well as the wallet credited.
close_reason:
Fixed on main (audit V-115). Local 2,533 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped; Postgres 192/192.

The bead offered two designs and one of them cannot work: having the projection emit for replayed receives is impossible, because a replayed receive journals exactly what a fresh one does - the projection cannot tell them apart, so it would either duplicate the coordinator's event or replace it.

What shipped: the coordinator registers itself with SPVActor (SetCoordinatorForSPVMessage, the shape SetArcActorForSPVMessage already uses), and SPVActor answers it whenever no caller is waiting. That covers the restart AND the _maxParkedSenders eviction, where a live process forgets a caller and used to drop the answer with a log line. Only a VERDICT is announced: a receive that goes back to waiting for a header is not an outcome, and announcing one would tell an app its import failed about a receive that is fine.

Two more defects found on the way:

1. SPVActor replayed receives whose headers arrived while the node was down in its own preStart, which runs BEFORE the coordinator exists - so that credit was silent by construction and a coordinator reference alone would have fixed nothing. The replay moved to the registration. The mutation that puts it back in preStart is what proves the move was necessary. That path also had NO test before this change.

2. coordinatorEvents is a broadcast stream, so an event emitted with no listener is dropped - and an app using LibSpiffyActorSystem can only subscribe after initialize() returns, while everything reported at startup is emitted from preStart. Whether a startup report arrived was a race with the app's own .listen. Events emitted before anything listens are now kept (bounded at 256) and handed to the first listener, then the window closes. This was ALREADY true of V-112's unfinished-channel report.

Tests: the bead's own (park, restart, deliver the header, assert the event AND the credit), the headers-arrived-while-down case, a third pinning the verdict rule by delivering a receive with no reply target at all, and two in channel_startup_sweep_test for the buffer. Seven mutations, each failing alone.

One correction recorded in the audit row: the first mutation run read 'pass 2 fail 0' and that was not a green mutation but a SEGFAULT - the hung test tore an Isar instance down mid-flight and the process died at exit 134, so two tests never reported. Replacing Stream.first.timeout with the file's polling helper made the same mutation fail cleanly and by name.

title: A pendingHeader merkle proof that verifies once its header arrives is never confirmed: only _reviveProofs (orphaned/rejected) restores a confirmation
description: From libspiffy-fggl. SPVActor._recheckUnverifiedProofs marks a pendingHeader proof verified once the header syncs (_recheckProof returns null on success after _checkProof rewrites the row as verified), but it never issues ConfirmTransactionCommand. Only _reviveProofs does that, and only for proofs whose stored status was orphaned or rejected. So a transaction of ours whose proof arrived before its header does not settle when the header lands; it waits for ARC. Fix: extract the confirm/mark-available block of _reviveProofs and call it from the recheck path when a pendingHeader proof becomes verified. Adjacent to libspiffy-zvj part 1 (imports accepted before headers synced are never re-checked); consider doing both in one lane. Test: store a proof at a height whose header we lack, sync the header, assert the recorded transaction is confirmed with no ARC involvement.

Retention gap adjacent to libspiffy-0lx. Test: receive a BEEF whose ancestor proof is at a height above our chain tip, sync the header, assert the transactions and proofs were retained and the receive now succeeds without the counterparty re-sending.

title: Trim merged BRC-74 BUMPs: leaves recomputable from the level below are kept, costing bytes in scattered-position cases
description: From libspiffy-0lx part 2 (V-66), deliberately not done. After merging the BUMPs of ancestors from one block, some leaves are recomputable from the level below (two ancestors at positions 0 and 2 of a 4-leaf block make both level-1 leaves redundant). The BSV TS SDK trims these and its computeRoot recomputes a missing sibling on the fly; our BUMP.computeMerkleRoot errors on a missing sibling, so trimming would need a find-or-compute step AND confidence that recipients do the same. An untrimmed merged BUMP is never larger than the unmerged pair and is verifiable under the strictest reading of BRC-74, which is why it was left. Also: BUMP.merge does not itself check that the merged paths share a merkle root (BeefBumps checks around it); if BUMP.merge gains other callers, move the check inside. Test must validate every leaf through the receiving path, not just measure size.

title: Reclaim a deferred payment by spending its held inputs back to the wallet, so the recipient's signed copy can never be mined
description:
Follow-up to libspiffy-7p2. CancelDeferredPaymentCommand releases the inputs but does not revoke the signed transaction the recipient holds. A ReclaimDeferredPaymentCommand builds a self-spend of the held inputs, broadcasts it via ARC, and resolves the deferred payment as reclaimed once the self-spend is seen (the original then fails as a double spend). Test: outstanding payment -> reclaim -> self-spend seen, original's later broadcast rejected, payment state reclaimed, balance restored minus fee.

DECIDED 2026-09-17 (user):
- FEE: standard ARC policy fee. Nothing else. This is Bitcoin SV: there is no replace-by-fee, so a conflicting transaction cannot displace ours by paying more, and ours cannot displace theirs. First seen wins. There is no race and no front-running, so no fee bump, no fee escalation, no caller fee override for 'winning', and no language in docs or API calling reclaim a race or best-effort. See spv-understanding.md Critical Implementation Note 3.
- CONFIRMATION: one-shot. The command builds and broadcasts. libspiffy does not own confirmation UX; the app decides whether to warn the user first. Document plainly that the command is immediate and that the recipient's signed copy is invalidated by it.
close_reason: Merged to main: cq16 as V-68 (counterparty marker, migration v021), 87a as V-69 (reclaim at policy fee, no migration). Both mutation-verified on main. Full suite 2,227 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped; Postgres 165/165.

title: Bare multisig and P2PK wallet UTXOs cannot fund a channel or a plugin transaction
description:
From libspiffy-nlp: channel funding (BuildFundingTransactionCommand), ProvisionFundingMessage and TransactionBuilderPlugin payments sign every input as P2PKH, so they exclude bare multisig and P2PK UTXOs (needsNonP2pkhUnlock). Sign those inputs with their own unlocking scripts (as SignTransactionCommand now does) so they can fund these too.

PATH A (channel funding) DONE 2026-09-18 as V-83 (commit dc2e297). The unlock decision now lives in one shared place, WalletTransactionSigner.unlockFor, used by both SignTransactionCommand and ChannelFunding.build. Two fee underpayments and one misreported reply were found and fixed on the way.

PATHS B AND C STILL OPEN, and they are NOT a selection bug: in both, the transaction's input is built by a third-party TransactionBuilderPlugin, not by libspiffy. PluginTransactionRequest hands the plugin fundingUtxos and one SVPublicKey each, and the plugin calls spendFromOutpointWithSigner(..., P2PKHUnlockBuilder(...)) - it chooses the unlocking script, and typically also rebuilds the LOCKING script as P2PKH from utxo.address rather than using utxo.scriptPubKey. libspiffy cannot make it emit OP_0 <sig>... or <sig>. Dropping the exclusion would hand plugins outputs they would sign over the wrong subscript and unlock with the wrong script - an invalid transaction instead of a clear refusal, which is strictly worse. The guard stays, with the reason documented at both sites in payment_coordinator_actor.dart.

What B and C need (see the new plugin-contract bead): extend PluginTransactionRequest with per-funding-UTXO unlocking-script builder FACTORIES (factories, not instances - buildWithSigner re-runs build across passes and instances would accumulate signatures), plus an opt-in on TransactionBuilderPlugin so plugins that do not implement it keep getting P2PKH-only funding.

Verified while there (the brief asked): aggregate_signing_client._ownerOf already resolves owners for bare-multisig and P2PK subscripts - it scans every push and accepts a 20-byte hash or a 33/65-byte key. It is NOT sufficient for m-of-n with m >= 2, because buildWithSigner caches signatures by 'sighashType:digest', so a second signer.sign() on the same input returns the same signature. That needs a per-signature cache key in _AggregateBackedSigner.

title: UpdateUTXOConfirmationsCommand accepts a caller-supplied blockHeight with no proof behind it
description:
Found by the libspiffy-4dja lane (V-71); severity established 2026-09-18 by reading the apply path.

THE ACTUAL EFFECT, which is worse than 'a misleading height': BitcoinUtxo.updateConfirmations promotes a UTXO whose status is pending - or voided - to AVAILABLE whenever confirmations > 0. UpdateUTXOConfirmationsCommand takes confirmations and blockHeight straight from the caller with no validation of any kind. So one command, with no proof anywhere, MAKES FUNDS SPENDABLE. That is exactly the scenario libspiffy-5ry (V-60) was created to prevent - 'a height a caller hands us is a claim, not evidence, and deriving available from it would conjure spendable funds without a proof' - and it also un-voids an output that libspiffy-3arz (V-73) designed to be revivable only by a proof that outranks the resolution.

EXPOSURE (corrected): it is NOT in libspiffy.dart or coordinator.dart. It is exported only from internals.dart, which states it is for 'building custom actors, extending aggregates, or writing integration tests'. I first filed this P2 claiming public-API reach without checking, then lowered it to P3 on the corrected exposure; it is back at P2 on the severity above - conjuring spendable funds is not a P3 whatever library the door is in. ReceiveUTXOCommand, which V-60 guarded, has exactly the same exposure, so the precedent was set on a command no more public than this one.

THE RULE TO ENFORCE: a caller-supplied confirmation count or height must not change spendability. Availability comes from MarkUTXOAvailableCommand (driven by ARC/SPV) or from a confirmation verified against our own header chain - never from this command.

Also: UtxoLedger.updateConfirmations writes 'blockHeight: command.blockHeight ?? 0', so an absent height is journaled as height 0, the genesis block, rather than null. Wrong independently of the proof question; fix it here.

ALSO CONSIDER WHETHER THIS COMMAND SHOULD EXIST. V-71 decided the wallet does NOT store a confirmation count - it derives one (tip height - blockHeight + 1) - because a stored count is stale at the next block. Nothing in lib/ sends this command; only tests. So before adding validation, check whether anything still needs it. Deprecate rather than delete (public API, even in internals).

BLAST RADIUS: 14 call sites in 9 test files, 11 of them passing confirmations > 0 and so relying on the promotion. Two are CHARACTERIZATION tests (aggregate_state_characterization_test.dart, wallet_aggregate_decomposition_characterization_test.dart) that deliberately pin current behaviour - update them deliberately, do not delete the coverage.

Test: the command cannot make a pending or voided UTXO spendable; an absent height is not journaled as 0.
close_reason: Merged to main as V-78. Command deprecated (nothing sends it); the promotion is gone from the apply path, closing three promotions not one; blockHeight nullable so an absent height is not the genesis block. Mutation-verified on main. Full suite 2,278 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped; Postgres 168/168.

title: Ask a counterparty for a fresh merkle proof when an ancestor's block is orphaned (the peer request message the 0lx state now needs)
description:
From libspiffy-0lx part 1 (V-65). The wallet now names each output waiting on an ancestor's proof (getOutputsAwaitingAncestorProof) but has no way to ask for one. The ARC route was removed deliberately: an ARC instance answers only for transactions submitted through it, so it has no standing to prove a counterparty's transaction, and a NOT_FOUND from it means nothing. Supplying the proofs its ancestry needs is the SENDER's obligation. The remaining legitimate source is therefore the counterparty who gave us the ancestor, and the library has no peer message to ask them. Add the request (and the coordinator command to trigger it), following the P2P model: we ask, they supply a BEEF with a fresh BUMP, we verify it against our own headers before storing. Do not add block scanning, address monitoring, or any third-party proof lookup. This is now the ONLY recovery route for an orphaned ancestor other than the block returning to the active chain, which is why it is P2. Test: an ancestor's block is orphaned, the counterparty is asked, supplies a fresh proof, the output becomes spendable.

DECIDED 2026-09-17 (user):
- WHO TO ASK: the counterparty marker recorded by libspiffy-cq16 (this bead now depends on it). The wallet stores an app-chosen opaque marker on every payment, so an OutputAwaitingProof can name the counterparty to ask.
- TRANSPORT: none of libspiffy's business. Follow the existing ChannelP2PAdapter precedent exactly - transport-agnostic, raw 'String messageType / Map payload' in and out, host app carries the bytes. New message types proof_request / proof_response; inbound arrives as a coordinator command, outbound as a CoordinatorEvent the app is expected to deliver. Do NOT add a socket, a client, or any network dependency.
- The response is verified against our OWN header chain before storing, like every other proof. A proof_response that does not verify is rejected and the output stays awaiting.
close_reason: Merged to main as V-70. Both halves of the proof_request/proof_response protocol over the app's own transport, no migration. Mutation-verified on main: unverified response reported as success, response-side marker check dropped, unnamed-peer guard removed. Full suite 2,234 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped; Postgres 165/165.

title: A wallet frozen by a journaled deferred hold reports a bare 'no funds' and no reserved balance
description:
Found 2026-09-19 by the libspiffy-z5uo lane (V-102), verified both halves.

When a channel funding (or any deferSpend payment) holds a wallet's inputs, the money leaves availableBalance entirely and lands in reservedBalance. The app is told neither fact.

(1) BalanceResponse (coordinator_messages.dart) carries confirmedBalance, unconfirmedBalance, totalBalance and watchOnlyBalance, and has NO reserved field - although WalletState.reservedBalance exists and the read-model wallet row already stores 'reservedBalance' and 'reservedUtxoCount' (wallet_projection.dart:1140,1147). So through the supported actor API a reserved UTXO simply vanishes from every reported number. Adding the field is additive and breaks nothing.

(2) WalletBalances.noneSelectableReason (wallet_balances.dart:185-220) builds its candidate list with utxo.status == UTXOStatus.available (:192). A journaled hold makes the UTXO 'reserved', so it is dropped BEFORE any reason is computed and the function returns the bare noneMessage. The branch at :208-212 that exists to say 'inputs of a deferred payment, held until it settles' reads legacyDeferredHeldKeys only, so it can never fire for a journaled hold - it covers only the legacy inferred holds, which leave the UTXO available.

EXTRA FINDING to fold in: ChannelFunding._noCandidatesReason (lib/src/core/wallet/channel_funding.dart:93-97) passes held: (u) => deferred.holderOf(state, u.key) != null specifically to narrow this diagnosis. For a journaled hold that predicate is DEAD CODE, because :192 already excluded the UTXO. So the channel-funding path's own 'no candidates' message is silent for exactly the case it was added for.

Why this was not done in the z5uo lane: part (2) is not a small additive change. noneSelectableReason is shared by channel funding and the Benford split precisely so the two cannot diagnose a wallet differently, its strings are pinned by tests, and the fix means admitting reserved UTXOs into the walk and ordering a new reason against the existing ones. A reservedBalance number without a reason is half an answer, so the two belong in one bead.

Note the money is already discoverable via GetDeferredPaymentsQuery, which lists the payment with its purpose and heldInputs - this bead is about the wallet's own balance API telling the truth, not about the money being lost.

Test: a wallet whose only funds are a stuck channel funding reports a reserved balance, and is told by name that its inputs are held by a deferred payment rather than that it has no funds.

title: Decide whether ReceiveUTXOCommand should refuse a P2PK output locked to a foreign key
description:
Raised by the libspiffy-kfvv lane (V-93) as a design question V-83 and V-93 did not settle.

UtxoLedger.receive checks a bare multisig script's keys (rejectMultisigNotSpendableAlone) but does NOT check a P2PK script's key, and does not require ReceiveUTXOCommand.address to match scriptPubKey at all. The mismatch is sometimes deliberate: payment_coordinator_actor.dart (around line 1509) builds an earmark output where the address and the script differ on purpose.

So a P2PK output locked to a key the wallet does not hold can be attributed to a wallet at receive time. V-93 made the library record such a row honestly and never spend it - the conservative answer. The stricter answer is to refuse it at the door, as an unmeetable bare multisig is refused.

DECIDE which, and record the reasoning either way:
- Refusing at receive is a stronger guarantee but risks rejecting an output an app legitimately wants tracked (the earmark precedent shows address/script mismatch is a real pattern here).
- Accepting and never spending keeps the honest record and costs a permanently unspendable row.

Note that whichever is chosen, REPLAY must keep accepting such rows: applyReceived validates no script deliberately (pinned by test/core/wallet_output_ownership_test.dart:227), because a journal written before any guard existed is still the record. A guard at receive is a command-path guard only.
close_reason: Decided and fixed on main as V-97: refuse at receive, as an unmeetable multisig already is. Watch addresses still accepted; replay unchanged.

title: A wallet created before the H4/xpub changes can never generate another address
description:
Split out of libspiffy-3gd (item 2) by the 19 Sep triage. THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS PARTLY WRONG and the correction matters for the fix.

wallet_keys.dart:278-281 reads the HD public key from secure storage and throws when it is absent:
  final xpubkey = await secureStorage.getString(hdPubKeyKey(command.walletId));
  if (xpubkey == null) throw StateError('HD public key not found for wallet ...');

It fails LOUDLY and permanently - it does not silently lack a pubkey. Any HD/XPRIV/XPUB wallet whose 'wallet_hdpubkey_<id>' key is missing can never derive another address, for the life of the wallet. There is no backfill anywhere: grep for backfill in lib/ finds only Postgres column backfills (v008, v023), nothing for secure storage.

THREE DISTINCT LEGACY COHORTS, and the original bead title only describes the second:
(1) Wallets created before 6e73584 ('initial implementation of xpub-only wallet support'): WalletCreatedEvent had NO hdPublicKeyXpub field at all. For these the bead's premise - 'backfill from the old WalletCreatedEvent xpub' - is FALSE. The xpub is nowhere in the journal and must be RE-DERIVED from wallet_xpriv_ / wallet_mnemonic_ in secure storage. That derivation already exists for private keys at wallet_keys.dart:417-444.
(2) Wallets created between 6e73584 and edc0951 (KM-8): the xpub IS in the journal payload, and WalletCreatedEvent.fromMap still reads it into the deprecated field (wallet_events.dart:78-81). This is the genuine backfill-from-the-event cohort.
(3) A narrower window before cb9e5b9 (H4): key material was written AFTER the event persisted, so a crash in between leaves a journaled wallet with no secret at all - neither xpub nor xpriv. Recovery may be impossible for these; decide what an honest answer looks like (a clear error naming the cause beats a bare StateError).

The fix needs a decision on source of truth: journal xpub, re-derive from xpriv/mnemonic, or both with a documented precedence. It touches the key-material invariant H4 established, so it should not be done casually.

TEST COVERAGE GAP THAT HID THIS: test/core/wallet_created_xpub_journal_test.dart:142 SEEDS wallet_hdpubkey_ before its legacy-replay test, so the missing-key case is never exercised. bitcoin_wallet_aggregate_key_material_test.dart:146 only asserts the key is present after a fresh create.

Fail-first test is clean: journal a WalletCreatedEvent with no wallet_hdpubkey_ in secure storage, replay, send GenerateAddressCommand, watch it throw.

No Postgres/Isar schema change - this is a secure-storage data migration, one-time or lazy-on-read.
close_reason: Fixed as V-107: WalletKeys.accountXpub recovers the account xpub from wallet_xpub_/wallet_xpriv_/wallet_mnemonic_ when wallet_hdpubkey_ is missing, verifies it against the journaled root address before trusting it (a lost BIP39 passphrase would otherwise derive a different wallet and hand out unsignable addresses), writes the verified key back, and names every key it looked for when nothing can be recovered. NOTE: the bead's cohort premise was wrong - wallet_hdpubkey_ has been written at creation since the first commit 4fd3822, so the journal-backfill cohort is empty and no release ever created a wallet without the key; what remains is the H4 crash window and host-side secure-storage moves.

title: Payment channel funding and settlement records carry no counterparty marker
description:
Follow-up from the libspiffy-cq16 lane (V-68).

Every payment the wallet records should carry a marker identifying the counterparty it was with, in both directions (spv-understanding.md, Core Data Management requirement 5). PaymentChannelManagerActor's funding recording currently records a null marker. The channel already knows its counterparty - PaymentChannel.counterpartyPeerId, and counterpartyPubKeyHex - so the peer id is available as a fallback.

The cq16 lane left them null rather than guess, which was the right call at the time: inventing a marker is worse than recording none. This bead is the deliberate decision to fill them in.

DECIDED 2026-09-18 by the owner: the app supplies the marker, with the counterparty peer id as the FALLBACK. Rationale: the marker is app-chosen and opaque everywhere else, and if the library picked peer ids for channel rows only, a marker would mean different things on different transaction types - an app filtering by its own identity strings would find libspiffy-chosen peer ids it does not recognise. Falling back to the peer id (a fact the library actually knows, never an invention) keeps channel transactions from being blank for apps that do not opt in.

Scope discovered by the 2026-09-18 survey:
- An app-supplied marker cannot reach the recording site today. The only string that reaches the aggregate is 'context', threaded coord.OpenChannelCommand (coordinator_messages.dart:801-824) -> wallet_coordinator_actor.dart:282 -> channel_p2p_adapter.dart:792-813 -> InitiateChannelMessage (payment_channel_messages.dart:15-36) -> payment_channel_manager_actor.dart:379-470 -> RequestChannelCommand (channel_commands.dart:31-72) -> ChannelRequestedEvent. A marker needs a new optional field through those five types, plus the event map/fromMap, and it must be journaled in channel state to survive a restart (PCMA never loads a PaymentChannel; it reads FullChannelStateResponse). AcceptChannelCommand (coordinator_messages.dart:897-925) has no context field at all, so the server side needs its own path.
- If the marker must survive in the channel read model, that is a Postgres migration and an Isar regeneration on top.
- The funding recording site is payment_channel_manager_actor.dart ~1432-1455 (RecordOutgoingTransactionCommand, no counterpartyMarker argument, defaults null).
- SpendUTXOCommand carries no marker field at all; only ReceiveUTXOCommand, RecordImportedTransactionCommand and RecordOutgoingTransactionCommand have one. Decide whether that matters here.
- THE SETTLEMENT HALF DOES NOT EXIST: close/expire record nothing in the wallet at all. See libspiffy-f5p2, which blocks it.

Test: open a channel with an app-supplied marker and fund it, then read the marker back off the funding transaction; and open one without, and read the peer id back.
close_reason:
Fixed as V-98 (commit ecdb0ce). Channel funding, settlement and refund records now carry a counterparty marker: the app's when it supplies one, the channel's counterparty peer id otherwise (client -> serverPeerId, server -> clientPeerId). One helper, _counterpartyMarkerFor, resolves the rule and both recording sites call it, so a channel's funding leg and its return leg can never be stamped differently.

Two corrections to the bead's own scope. (1) The bead said an app-supplied string cannot reach the recording site and budgeted a new field through five types; the survey found 'context' already threads that whole path (OpenChannelCommand -> InitiateChannelMessage -> RequestChannelCommand -> ChannelRequestedEvent -> ChannelState -> FullChannelStateResponse). It was still NOT reused: PCMA consumes 'context' as address-derivation metadata (metadata: {'context': ...} on GenerateAddressCommand), so an app labelling its addresses would silently find that string stamped as the counterparty on every channel transaction - one field, two meanings, which is the confusion the owner's own rationale rejected. counterpartyMarker is a separate optional field. (2) The bead flagged a possible Postgres migration and Isar regeneration if the marker must survive in the channel read model. It need not: requirement 5 is about the wallet's payment rows, which now carry it; the journal and snapshot carry it for restart; and payment_channels already holds both peer ids. No migration was written, and Postgres stayed 178/178.

The marker is taken from the local AcceptChannelCommand, never from the inbound peer's payload - it is the app's own naming of its counterparty, not something a peer supplies.

title: Record a counterparty identity marker on every payment, incoming and outgoing
description:
The wallet must store a marker identifying the counterparty on every payment it records, in BOTH directions. The marker is an opaque string chosen by the app (Ed25519 identity key, email address, peer id, internal account id): libspiffy does not interpret or validate it. It is a marker, NOT an identity record - names, contacts, key material and verification state stay with the app. Retained like all other wallet data: never deleted, never overwritten.

Today fromCounterparty is accepted by ReceiveTransactionCommand but only persisted on PARKED receives (PendingReceive, bead libspiffy-vfai). A transaction that received cleanly keeps no record of who sent it, and outgoing payments have no counterparty field at all. That gap is what blocks libspiffy-a2v3: when an ancestor's block is orphaned we cannot tell who to ask for a fresh proof.

Scope: read-model column + migration v021 on all three backends (in-memory, Isar, Postgres), aggregate/journal event carrying the marker, exposed on transaction queries. Outgoing side needs the marker plumbed through the send path. Test: receive with a marker and read it back after a restart; send with a marker and read it back; an orphaned ancestor's OutputAwaitingProof can name the counterparty to ask.
close_reason: Merged to main: cq16 as V-68 (counterparty marker, migration v021), 87a as V-69 (reclaim at policy fee, no migration). Both mutation-verified on main. Full suite 2,227 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped; Postgres 165/165.

title: Wave 3 lane 5 follow-ups: RefundClaimedEvent.refundTxId not projected to the read model; no refund-claim flow creates ClaimRefundCommand; payment_channels.lock_time_unix INTEGER overflows after 2038
description:
Wave 3 lane 5 follow-ups, three parts.

(a) RefundClaimedEvent.refundTxId not projected to the read model — DONE 2026-09-18 as V-81 (commit fdb92c3). Recorded into the existing settlementTxId column; a closing txid is now written once and never replaced on all three closing routes, and a conflicting second txid is logged rather than dropped.

(c) payment_channels.lock_time_unix INTEGER overflows after 2038 — DONE 2026-09-18 as V-81. Postgres migration v022 widens it to BIGINT; Isar and in-memory were already 64-bit (confirmed by contract test on all three backends).

(b) STILL OPEN: no refund-claim flow creates ClaimRefundCommand. The command exists on the aggregate (channel_commands.dart:562-583, handler payment_channel_aggregate.dart:1098-1150) and is constructed only in tests. A claim flow needs a message in payment_channel_messages.dart, a handler in PaymentChannelManagerActor, a public command in coordinator_messages.dart and dispatch in wallet_coordinator_actor.dart + channel_p2p_adapter.dart — mirroring the expiry path exactly — plus an ARC broadcast like _fundClientChannel. The refund hex it needs is already in state (FullChannelStateResponse.signedRefundTxHex). The read model is now ready for it.

Part (b) is deliberately grouped with libspiffy-1n3 (retry funding / re-send channel_open) for a later round: both add a public command through the same coordinator_messages -> wallet_coordinator_actor -> adapter seam, and authoring them in separate lanes would collide.
close_reason:
All three parts now done; closing the bead. (a) and (c) were V-81 (commit fdb92c3). Part (b) is fixed as V-99 (commit ecdb0ce).

Part (b): ClaimRefundCommand had an aggregate handler, tested guards, a journal event and a projection arm, and nothing in lib/ ever built it - one of the three dead commands that prompted the V-87 reachability sweep. A client whose counterparty had gone silent held a fully signed refund with no way to broadcast it. New public ClaimChannelRefundCommand -> WalletCoordinatorActor dispatch -> ChannelP2PAdapter.handleClaimRefund (a plain forwarder, not _sequenced: the claim needs nothing from the adapter's per-channel cache, exactly like close and expire) -> ClaimRefundMessage -> PCMA._handleClaimRefund.

It runs the expiry path plus the one thing expiry deliberately does not do: a broadcast. Order is broadcast, then journal, then record the wallet - a claim is a claim about the network, so nothing the network refused is journaled as claimed. A rejection (most likely the counterparty's settlement having reached the network first) is terminal, reported on the response, never retried at a higher fee: there is no replace-by-fee on BSV. ARC is asked because the refund is our own transaction.

The convergence question the bead predates: V-86 made expiry record the return leg WITHOUT broadcasting, so two routes can now record the same refund. Both orderings are pinned by tests. expire-then-claim skips the wallet write on returnLegRecordedInWallet and contributes the broadcast; claim-then-expire short-circuits in _handleExpireChannel and journals no ChannelExpiredEvent. One wallet row and one RefundClaimedEvent either way.

One guard was missing and is added: the aggregate accepted a refund claim on a cooperatively closed (or rejected) channel, journaling a second ending for a funding output the settlement had already spent, behind a broadcast the network would refuse as a double spend. 'expired' stays claimable, because that is the convergence path.

Test: test/actors/payment_channel_refund_claim_test.dart, 11 tests. Three mutations verified on main, including the RefundClaimedEvent projection arm - pre-existing code that no test pinned until now.

Left open and filed separately: a repeated claim journals a second RefundClaimedEvent, because the aggregate records no claim and so cannot refuse one.

title: Follow-up cleanups: Isar (status, statusChangedAt) index and old-store test for competingTxids; stale docs; split response counts; storeWallet merge doc
description: From the 16 Sep follow-up batch (V-52..V-55). (1) Isar has no (status, statusChangedAt) index for getMerkleProofsByStatusChangedSince (filters natively within status); add with a rows-read test. (2) No Isar test opens a store written before DeferredPaymentEntity.competingTxids. (3) utxo_ledger.dart and wallet_events.dart docs still say the Benford coordinator listens to UTXOSplitInitiatedEvent. (4) WalletCoordinatorActor._handleSplitUTXOsResponse sets transactionCount from splitCount and totalFeePaid 0. (5) A Benford split failing to build or sign before recording is skipped with no outcome in the reply. (6) BitcoinTransactionEntity.applyDomain doc says confirmedAt is set whenever there is a block height (storage overrides). (7) Postgres storeWallet replaces metadata_json while ReadModelStorage docs say it merges.
close_reason:
Triaged 19 Sep and split into five beads. Six of seven premises held; one was stated backwards. TWO ITEMS WERE BADLY MIS-PRIORITISED AT P4 and are now P2.

ITEM 7 IS NOT A DOC BUG - it is data loss, and I verified it directly. Postgres storeWallet does metadata_json = COALESCE(@metadataJson, wallet_metadata.metadata_json), which REPLACES the whole JSON document; Isar (isar_wallet_storage.dart:135-138) and in-memory (:173-179) both MERGE, as ReadModelStorage:42-45 says every backend does. The in-memory backend's own comment even asserts 'as the Isar and Postgres backends do', which is false. Two tests run the identical scenario - wallet_storage_test.dart:115-142 asserts the merge, postgres_integration_test.dart:685-704 makes the same two calls and OMITS the metadata assertion. On Postgres that sequence drops version:1. Raised to P2.

ITEMS 4 AND 5 are one defect class and are now one P2 bead: the Benford split reply states things the code cannot evidence. A split failing to build or sign returns null and vanishes, so if every source fails the caller gets success:true with empty splits - a total failure reported as success. And transactionCount is fed from splitCount, which is a UTXO count (made.length * targetUtxoCount), so with the default targetUtxoCount:5 one transaction is reported as five. totalFeePaid:BigInt.zero is a manufactured value - the fee is computed then discarded and never plumbed to the reply.

ITEM 6's PREMISE IS INVERTED - the sixth wrong-premise bead here. The bead says the doc claims confirmedAt is set whenever there is a block height; the doc says the opposite ('set once ... not cleared') and it is the CODE that does 'whenever'. Moot either way: both backends override it via TransactionRowRules.confirmedAtAfter, already contract-tested at transaction_status_contract.dart:237-277, so applyDomain's if-block is dead weight both callers overwrite.

ITEM 1 turns out to be doable under the project's no-wall-clock rule, which was the open question. Isar 3 has no query explain, but this repo built its own: IsarWalletStorage.onQuery plus _Trace.rowsInRange in isar_query_access_test.dart, which counts rows actually read. Also note Isar is the ODD BACKEND OUT - Postgres already has the index (v018), and read_model_storage.dart:620-621 states the index as a contract for all backends.

ITEM 2 is a legitimate close-as-wont-do candidate: the generated reader (libspiffy_schemas.g.dart:7069, readStringList(...) ?? []) makes the claim true by construction, and a property-level old-schema fixture has no precedent here - the three existing Isar migration tests are index-only and cannot be reused, because serialize/deserialize read by offsets derived from the property map.

Split out:
- P2: Postgres storeWallet replaces metadata_json while the other two merge (item 7)
- P2: Benford split reports outcomes it cannot evidence (items 4+5, merged)
- P3: Isar getMerkleProofsByStatusChangedSince has no (status, statusChangedAt) index (item 1)
- P4: doc-only sweep, with the item-6 premise inversion recorded (items 3+6)
- P4: no Isar old-store test for competingTxids, with the wont-do argument written down (item 2)

title: Aggregate snapshots record a Dart class name as state_type; give State subclasses a stable typeName before anything reads it
description:
Split out of libspiffy-3gd (item 1) by the 19 Sep triage. PREMISE HALF TRUE - the correction is that this is prophylactic hardening, not a live defect.

TRUE: the class name really is stored. eventador's State.typeName is 'String get typeName => runtimeType.toString();' and its own doc names the hazard: 'Defaults to the Dart class name, which breaks on rename or under --obfuscate; override it with a name that never changes.' None of libspiffy's three State subclasses override it - ChannelState, InvoiceState, WalletState. The stableTypeName pattern exists for EVENTS only.

It is written in three places: the Postgres snapshot_envelopes.state_type column (postgres_event_store.dart:487-488), the Isar SnapshotEnvelope.stateType, and the 'type' key of the snapshot payload for channel and invoice (payment_channel_aggregate.dart:64, invoice_aggregate.dart:71). Note WalletState.toMap does not call super.toMap(), so the wallet snapshot payload has no 'type' key at all - only the storage column carries it.

THE CORRECTION: the stored value is NEVER READ FOR DISPATCH, so a rename does not break restore today.
- PostgresEventStore.loadSnapshot passes state_type to CborSerializer.deserializeState, which IGNORES the argument except in an error message.
- StateRegistry - which does key on typeName and does have registerAlias - has ZERO references in libspiffy.
- Restore goes AggregateRoot.onSnapshot -> restoreFromSnapshot -> restoreStateFromMap, and all three libspiffy overrides read fields by name and never read map['type'].

So the exposure is: (a) the stored label is wrong-forever under --obfuscate or after a rename, and (b) the day anything starts using StateRegistry.fromMap, or queries/filters on state_type, every old snapshot is silently orphaned.

Fix: three one-line typeName overrides plus a golden-name test mirroring test/core/event_type_names_test.dart (411 lines, goldenTypeNames table at :18-60). Note a golden table added AFTER the overrides passes trivially - the honest fail-first is 'a renamed class keeps its stored state_type', which needs a rename simulation. Say which you did.

No schema migration. Existing snapshot rows keep 'WalletState'/'ChannelState'/'InvoiceState' in state_type, which is harmless today and would need an alias table only if something starts reading it.

P4 because nothing is broken now. Worth doing BEFORE anything begins reading state_type - after that it is a data migration instead of a one-line override.

title: TransactionBroadcastEvent journals the constant 'broadcast_success', never ARC's answer
description:
Found by the libspiffy-1kd5 reachability sweep; see doc/reachability-sweep-2026-09-18.md section 4, D-2.

outgoing_transactions.dart:587

  broadcastResponse: 'broadcast_success', // Placeholder - will be set by ARC service

Every TransactionBroadcastEvent ever journaled carries that literal. BroadcastTransactionCommand has no field to carry what ARC actually answered, so the ARC service never does set it, and the comment promises a wiring that does not exist.

Nothing downstream is wrong today: all four senders (arc_actor.dart:397, 465, 529, 1356) send the command only after submitTransaction returns, and ARC's real status is recorded separately via UpdateTransactionStatusCommand -> TransactionStatusUpdatedEvent -> projection. But a fabricated field sits permanently in an immutable journal, which is the same species as V-78, V-79, V-80 and V-86: where evidence is missing the honest record is an absence, not a plausible value.

FIX: add an optional response field to BroadcastTransactionCommand (additive), have arc_actor pass ARC's actual answer, and have OutgoingTransactions.broadcast record what it was given. Where the caller supplies nothing, record an absence rather than 'broadcast_success'. The event field itself cannot simply be deleted: TransactionBroadcastEvent is registered for replay and existing journals contain it.

TEST: drive BroadcastTransactionCommand with a known ARC response and assert the journaled event carries it; on the code as found the event always reads broadcast_success.

title: Closing or expiring a payment channel records no settlement transaction in the wallet
description:
Found 2026-09-18 by the survey for the channel-cluster round (while sizing libspiffy-bps1, which assumes a settlement recording exists).

PaymentChannelManagerActor writes to the wallet in exactly two places: _recordFundingInWallet (~1415-1475, RecordOutgoingTransactionCommand) and the input-spend loop (~1485-1556, SpendUTXOCommand). Both are on the funding path.

_handleCloseChannel (~1777-1809) and _handleExpireChannel (~1816-1860) journal CHANNEL events only and tell the wallet nothing. FinalizeCloseCommand (channel_commands.dart:505-530) is constructed nowhere in lib/ - only in tests. So when a channel settles or expires, the settlement or refund transaction never reaches the wallet's transaction history, its outputs never become wallet UTXOs, and the balance does not reflect the funds coming back.

That is a data-retention failure in the sense spv-understanding.md means: the transaction exists, we have it, and we drop it. It also means the channel's money is invisible to the wallet after settlement.

Related: libspiffy-cqc (b) records that no flow constructs ClaimRefundCommand either - the same shape of gap on the refund path. Both are 'the aggregate can do it, nothing asks it to'.

Scope: decide what a settling/expiring channel should record in the wallet (the settlement transaction, its outputs, the spend of the funding output) and make close/expire do it. Check whether FinalizeCloseCommand is the right vehicle or dead weight to remove. Note this blocks the settlement half of libspiffy-bps1 (a counterparty marker on a recording that does not exist yet).

Test: fund, pay, close a channel, then read the settlement transaction and its outputs back off the wallet.
close_reason: Fixed as V-86 (commit aa7642d). Close and expiry now record the return leg in the wallet as an unproven receive (the funding output is not a wallet UTXO, so a settlement creates wallet outputs and spends no wallet input). Two defects fixed on the way: the fully signed settlement was never assembled (fullySignedPaymentTxHex: '' with a 'simplified for now' comment), and FinalizeCloseCommand was constructed nowhere, so a cooperative close hung in 'closing' forever with ChannelClosedEvent unreachable. Test: test/actors/payment_channel_manager_settlement_test.dart. One gap remains, filed separately: a client never holds a cooperative settlement.

title: A rejected payment_update tells the client nothing: no payment_ack, no channel_error
description:
Found 2026-09-18 by the libspiffy-kyw lane (V-82), same family as kyw (b) but on the payment path rather than the open path.

ChannelP2PAdapter._handlePaymentUpdate (~445-464) tells AcknowledgePaymentMessage with NO sender, so when the aggregate refuses the payment the response goes nowhere: no payment_ack, no channel_error, nothing. The client is left waiting for an acknowledgement that will never come, with no way to tell a refusal from a lost message.

Not fixed in V-82 because it needs a reply target on that message, not just an extra send - the lane left it rather than reshaping the message in a hardening pass.

title: A BEEF with a proof for a transaction the wallet recorded leaves its deferred payment 'seen' instead of 'mined' and its change output pending
description:
A merkle proof delivered peer-to-peer inside a BEEF never confirms one of our own transactions. One rule is missing: a BUMP that verifies against our active header chain confirms that txid if the wallet recorded it, whatever position the transaction occupies in the BEEF.

Three defects, all on the BEEF receive path (SPVActor -> WalletManagerActor -> aggregate/projection):

(1) ANCESTOR PROOF FOR OUR OWN TX IS FILED AND IGNORED. When our outgoing deferred payment T is later handed back to us as an *ancestor* of a counterparty's new transaction (they spend the output T paid them), the BEEF carries T with a BUMP - the first hard evidence T was mined. spv_actor.dart:317-337 validates it; wallet_projection.dart:1064-1082 _storeAncestors writes the raw tx to the txid-keyed ancestor store and the proof via _storeMerkleProofFromBump, and stops. Nothing compares an ancestor txid against the wallet's own recorded transactions (wallet_manager_actor.dart:577-665 uses only result.txid; _storeAncestors is wallet-agnostic). The deferred payment stays outstanding. If the incoming subject also spends our UTXOs, SpendUTXOCommand -> UTXOSpentEvent -> deferred_payments.dart:405 marks the payment 'seen' - a weak inference standing in for the proof we were just handed.
Root cause: deferred_payments.dart:414 applyConfirmed (the only route to 'mined') runs only from TransactionConfirmedEvent, i.e. only from ConfirmTransactionCommand, whose only two producers are arc_actor.dart:963 (ARC MINED) and spv_actor.dart:1282 (_reviveProofs, and only for proofs stored orphaned/rejected). A freshly stored ancestor proof is verified/pendingHeader, so it feeds neither. Only ARC can mine a payment - which inverts the P2P SPV model.

(2) AGGREGATE AND READ MODEL DIVERGE when the BEEF's SUBJECT is a txid we already recorded outgoing and carries a BUMP. wallet_projection.dart:996 flips the read-model row to confirmed (TransactionRowRules.setsStatus allows it), but no TransactionConfirmedEvent is journaled, so the aggregate's deferred record never reaches 'mined' and its inputs stay held. The wallet displays confirmed while the write model does not agree, until ARC independently reports MINED.

(3) THE PROVEN-SUBJECT BRANCH DISCARDS EVERY ANCESTOR. spv_actor.dart:285-306: if the subject carries its own BUMP, 'ancestors' stays empty and no other BEEF member is examined. Proofs a counterparty gave us are thrown away (retention), and the receipt case - counterparty returns our T with its proof - drops everything else. Interacts with libspiffy-0lx (orphaned ancestor, nothing refetches a proof).

Also: the duplicate change output fails silently. Our change output of T is already recorded, so ReceiveUTXOCommand hits utxo_ledger.dart:150-161 'UTXO $key already exists in wallet' (StateError), but wallet_manager_actor.dart:616 sends it via bare tell() with no sender, so there is no reply target and the throw is dropped. The change output sits pending and nothing reports why.

EXPECTED: match every proven txid in a received BEEF (subject and ancestor alike) against the wallet's recorded transactions, and issue ConfirmTransactionCommand with the BUMP for each hit. outgoing_transactions.confirm already journals the spend of held inputs, moves the payment to mined, and confirms the change output at the proven height. The subject's own outputs stay pending - a BEEF proof proves funding history, not settlement. Stop short-circuiting ancestor collection in the proven-subject branch. Make the duplicate-UTXO case a no-op or an update rather than a dropped throw.

TESTS FIRST (each must fail on d127c9b): (a) record a deferred payment T -> receive a BEEF whose subject is a counterparty tx and whose ancestor is T with a valid BUMP -> T confirmed, payment mined, change output available at the proven height, inputs spent; (b) receive a BEEF whose subject is T with a BUMP -> aggregate deferred record is mined, not just the read-model row; (c) receive a BEEF with a proven subject plus proven ancestors -> ancestor raw tx and proofs retained.
close_reason: Fixed on main. One rule: a BUMP that verifies against our active header chain confirms that txid if the wallet recorded it, wherever it sits in the BEEF (SPVValidationResult.provenTransactions, ConfirmTransactionCommand.onlyIfRecorded). Confirming also makes the transaction's own pending outputs available, so a deferred payment's change is spendable when the proof arrives. The proven-subject branch no longer discards the rest of the BEEF. A duplicate ReceiveUTXOCommand is a no-op, not a dropped StateError. Audit V-56. Seven mutation-verified tests in test/integration/beef_proof_confirms_recorded_test.dart, including a forged BUMP that must not settle a payment. Follow-ups filed separately.

title: The nullable lock time and version stop at the storage boundary, and backup/restore is unreachable
description:
Two follow-ups reported by the V-88 lane (libspiffy-zpu7).

1. THE HONEST int? STOPS AT THE STORAGE BOUNDARY. BitcoinTransaction.lockTime and .version are now int?, but RecordOutgoingTransactionCommand.txVersion/txLockTime and TransactionImportedEvent.txVersion/txLockTime are still non-nullable int. That is arguably right for the write path - at the moment we record a transaction we have just serialized it, so both are known - but it is currently enforced by a StateError added in payment_coordinator_actor._recordOutgoingTransaction rather than by the types. Decide: either say in the doc comments that the write path always knows them and keep the throw as a fail-closed assertion, or carry int? through the command and the event so the absence is expressible end to end. Do not leave it as an undocumented asymmetry.

Note the StateError is unreachable in practice today: every caller builds the record from hex it just serialized, and TransactionRowRules.intrinsicsOf recovers both fields from that hex.

2. BitcoinTransactionEntity.toJson / fromJson have no callers in lib/ or test/. They are the backup/restore pair. The V-88 lane fixed a real asymmetry in them on the way past (fromJson dropped counterpartyMarker while toJson wrote it, so a cq16 marker was lost on a round trip) - which is exactly the kind of defect unreachable code accumulates unnoticed. Decide whether backup/restore is a capability that should be reachable, or whether the pair should go. Related: libspiffy-vspy, the dead-type list from the same sweep.

title: Balance buckets still use a stored confirmations count, so proof-confirmed funds read as unconfirmed
description:
Found by the libspiffy-4dja lane (V-71); the half deliberately left out of scope there.

V-71 made a proof-confirmed UTXO carry the proven block height, and decided NOT to store a confirmation count: a stored count is stale at the very next block and nothing journals an event per block, so keeping one true would mean rewriting every UTXO of the wallet on every header. The count is tip height - blockHeight + 1 wherever it is wanted.

Two places still bucket on a stored count and so disagree with that:
- WalletBalances.bucketOf uses confirmations >= 6, so a proof-confirmed UTXO counts as UNCONFIRMED balance in the write model and in the read-model wallet row.
- WalletManagerActor (~wallet_manager_actor.dart:607) writes confirmations: 1 on a proven receive, and WalletProjection writes confirmations: 1 on a confirmed transaction row. Both are counts that never advance.

The honest fix is to bucket on the derived count, which needs a chain tip available to the aggregate - a design change touching the balance table in spv-understanding.md, which is why it was not folded into V-71. Note WalletCoordinatorActor._handleGetBalance already does the right thing (confirmed means blockHeight != null), so the two paths currently disagree with each other.

Decide the rule once, write it in spv-understanding.md, and make every site follow it.

No depth threshold; confirmedAt deleted. updateConfirmations lost its blockHeight parameter so the deprecated command structurally cannot record one. Fabricated counts removed. Mutation-verified on main. Full suite 2,294 pass / 0 fail / 2 skipped; Postgres 168/168.

title: A P2PK output to a key the wallet does not hold may count in the read-side spendable balance
description:

The aggregate's _unlocksAlone (channel_funding.dart, V-83) excludes a P2PK output locked to a key the wallet does not hold. The read side does not have the same rule: splitBalanceUtxos / isWatchOnlyOutput catch such an output only when its address is a registered watch address.

So a P2PK row attributed to a wallet but locked to a foreign key could be counted in the read-side spendable balance while funding refuses to spend it - the two layers disagreeing about the same output, which is the class of defect V-79 closed for 'confirmed'.

The lane could not establish a path that attributes such a UTXO to a wallet in the first place (ReceiveUTXOCommand's ownership checks may already prevent it). So the first task is to decide whether the state is reachable at all.
