title: Untyped failure replies: WalletManagerActor Maps and both aggregates' Map/List replies must move to ActorResponse together
description:
Split out of libspiffy-ro84 (clusters A and B) by the 19 Sep triage. ONE bead because A and B ARE NOT SEPARABLE AT THE RECEIVE SIDE: six receivers discriminate on 'payload is Map' alone and cannot tell the two producers apart. Converting one producer leaves the is-Map branch live for the other and the receiver's own comment lying.

CLUSTER A - WalletManagerActor, 3 send sites (the only bare-Map LocalMessages in lib/src/actors + lib/src/core besides the aggregates):
  wallet_manager_actor.dart:286 catch-all {'error', 'type': 'wallet_manager_error'} - fires for ANY unhandled throw in any branch
  :426 {'error': 'Wallet not found', 'walletId'} - wallet has no journal
  :435 {'error': e.toString(), 'walletId'} - journal read/load failure
TEN receiver sites across 5 files (the bead implied one each): aggregate_signing_client.dart:522; payment_channel_manager_actor.dart:440, :535, :3023; payment_coordinator_actor.dart:1580, :1601 (the V-31 refusal receiver); benford_coordinator_actor.dart:702, :729; invoice_coordinator_actor.dart:119, :442.

Its four ask<wm.XResponse> sites (:813, :1153, :1270, :1329) would take a cast failure on the same map. Fix this as part of the work.

CLUSTER B1 - BitcoinWalletAggregate fallback, bitcoin_wallet_aggregate.dart:530-535, {'error', 'command'}. Blast radius: the typed chain (:429-529) covers 13 commands while wallet_commands.dart declares 35, so roughly 22 command types land in this fallback. Receivers are THE SAME SIX as cluster A - one receiver sees both the manager map and the aggregate map, which is precisely why these cannot be split.

CLUSTER B2 - PaymentChannelAggregate, and THIS IS THE RISKIEST PIECE:
  :279-283 failure {'success': false, 'error', 'commandId'}
  :262 success - a RAW List<Event>
Single funnel: payment_channel_manager_actor.dart._askAggregate (:283-296) with EIGHTEEN call sites.
THE LIST IS LOAD-BEARING - do not collapse it to success/error. All 18 sites feed it to _broadcastEvents (:254-266), which forwards the typed ChannelEvent instances to the external P2P broadcaster. :485 reads a field off a specific event (whereType<ChannelRequestedEvent>().single, then requested.lockTimeUnix, with a comment saying recomputing it locally would be wrong). title: Channel follow-ups from libspiffy-lhd: RecordPaymentCommand lacks amount > 0 guard; adapter sends no channel_error to the peer on server rejection; rejected open/expire leave projection awaiter until 10 s timeout
description:
Channel follow-ups from libspiffy-lhd, three parts.

(a) RecordPaymentCommand lacked an amount > 0 guard — DONE 2026-09-18 as V-82 (commit 5ef1395). Every other guard is inert against a negative amount: the insufficient-balance check cannot trigger, and the arithmetic RAISES the client balance and lowers the server's, so a client could journal a payment clawing back what it had already paid.

(b) The adapter sent no channel_error to the peer on server rejection — DONE 2026-09-18 as V-82. All four _reportFailure sites now tell the counterparty; an unknown channel is logged and nothing is sent.

(c) STILL OPEN: rejected open/expire leave a projection awaiter until the 10 s timeout. NOT fixable inside libspiffy as it stands. The awaiter lives in eventador's ProjectionActor (hosted eventador 3.0.0): its protocol has AwaitEventApplied, Pause/Resume/Rebuild/StopProjection and NO cancel primitive, and an unknown message is ignored, so PaymentChannelManagerActor has nothing to send that frees it. Registering after _askAggregate instead reintroduces the read-after-write race the pre-registration exists to close (overnode_v2-8gh): the aggregate publishes the event to the projection's mailbox before it answers, so a post-ask registration can miss it and then wait out the full 10 s on the SUCCESS path — strictly worse. AwaitEventApplied.alreadySatisfied cannot close the gap: it is a synchronous bool Function() evaluated inside the projection, and the manager has no synchronous way to know whether the projection applied the event.

What would fix it: add a cancel to eventador's ProjectionActor (AwaitEventApplied carrying a caller-chosen id, plus CancelAwait(id) removing the entry and cancelling its timer), then have _awaitApplied return a handle and both catch blocks (_handleOpenChannel, _handleExpireChannel) cancel it. A test would observe zero pending awaiters after a rejected open.

Impact today is bounded — one closure and one timer per rejected open/expire, for 10 s, self-clearing — but it is on a path a peer can drive with repeated bad channel_open messages. The lane declined to add an untestable no-op edit, which was the right call.
close_reason: All three parts done. (a) and (b) fixed as V-82 (commit 5ef1395): the amount>0 guard on RecordPaymentCommand, and channel_error to the peer on every failed step. (c) fixed as V-84 (commit 0433678): eventador gained CancelEventAwait (commit 36b30cf in ../eventador, unreleased), _awaitApplied returns a handle and both catch blocks cancel. Tests: test/actors/channel_await_cancel_test.dart plus four in eventador's projection_actor_test.dart. NOTE: libspiffy now builds against the local ../eventador via dependency_overrides until that release is published - see libspiffy-ppl5.

title: ProofP2PAdapter may match the wrong verdict when a receive and a proof response for the same txid are in flight together
description:
Found and reported by the libspiffy-a2v3 lane (V-70); narrow and benign, but real.

SPVActor's reply is not a dactor LocalMessage, so ActorRef.ask cannot be used for it ('Bad state: Ask response must be a LocalMessage'). ProofP2PAdapter therefore tells with sender: coordinator, and the coordinator hands SPVValidationResults back through ProofP2PAdapter.handleReceiveResult, matched FIFO per txid.

If an ordinary ReceiveTransactionCommand and a proof_response for the SAME txid are in flight at the same moment, the adapter may take the other one's verdict. Both are verdicts on that txid so the outcome is benign today, but the pairing is by arrival order rather than by identity, and that is the kind of thing that stops being benign when a third path starts receiving the same txid.

Fix direction: correlate the verdict to the request rather than to the txid (a correlation id carried through the receive message and echoed on the result), or make SPVActor's reply a LocalMessage so ask() can be used and the pairing is structural. The second is the larger change and would remove a workaround that exists in more than one place - worth checking how many callers would benefit before choosing.

title: Expiry journals its channel event before the wallet write, so a crash between them loses the settlement record

Found 2026-09-18 by the libspiffy-f5p2 lane (V-86).

The funding path already closed the equivalent hole with FundingRecordedInWalletEvent - the channel journal records that the wallet write happened, so a resumed funding knows whether to redo it. The close path got the same shape in V-86 via the resumable 'closing' state. Expiry has neither.

Fix: a SettlementRecordedInWalletEvent (or reuse the funding one's pattern) so an interrupted expiry can be resumed. It needs channel_state.dart and the channel read model, both outside the V-86 lane's file list, which is why it was reported rather than done.

title: PaymentChannelManagerActor's wallet read-model guard silently no-ops without storage
description:
Reported by the libspiffy-ymi6 lane (V-92).

PaymentChannelManagerActor._walletHoldsTransaction is a read-model check that is a NO-OP when the manager is built without a storage argument (tests, degraded configurations). V-92 gave the wallet aggregate its own guard, so a duplicate TransactionImportedEvent is no longer journaled in that configuration - the hole that mattered is closed.

What remains: in the same storage-less configuration the manager also skips the reasoning around _awaitApplied that depends on the read model, so a resumed close does more work than it needs to and its idempotency now rests entirely on the aggregate. That is safe but undocumented.

DECIDE: either make storage required (the manager cannot do its job honestly without it, and a silent no-op guard is the kind of thing this backlog keeps finding), or document at the constructor exactly which guarantees are dropped when it is absent. Do not leave a guard that silently does nothing.

Related: libspiffy-1kd5 (the reachability sweep) - a check that silently no-ops is the same species as a capability nothing reaches.
close_reason: Decided and shipped as V-111. m0xj: 'required' was tried empirically and does not fit yet (an empty read model is not behaviour-neutral; blocked on the fixture work in libspiffy-tg4d), so the other branch was done properly - the storage parameter documents each of the four guarantees that degrade, preStart warns when it is absent so the configuration is never silent, and _walletHoldsTransaction states that false means 'not known to'. yypk: 'every request is answered' is now a checkable property - every request type is driven into a failure and must answer in its own response type, with a coverage guard that reads onMessage's dispatch out of the source.

title: in_memory_event_store test helper treats fromSequence as inclusive; both real backends are exclusive
description:
Split out of libspiffy-3gd (item 3) by the 19 Sep triage. Premise true; it is a TEST HELPER, and the bug is latent.

test/actors/in_memory_event_store.dart:30-37:
  // Sequence numbers are 1-based journal positions.
  final start = fromSequence <= 1 ? 0 : fromSequence - 1;
So fromSequence: 1 returns event #1 and fromSequence: 2 returns event #2 - INCLUSIVE, off by one for every fromSequence >= 1.

Both real backends are EXCLUSIVE:
- Postgres: 'AND sequence_number > @fromSequence' (postgres_event_store.dart:373)
- Isar: persistenceIdEqualToSequenceNumberGreaterThan(...), and Between(..., includeLower: false)
And the project's OTHER in-memory store agrees with the real ones: test/core/aggregate_snapshot_restore_test.dart:57-62 uses events.sublist(fromSequence, end) with a header comment saying 'exclusive fromSequence'. So this helper is the odd one out, not the backends.

WHY IT IS LATENT: PersistentActor only passes a non-zero fromSequence after a successful loadSnapshot, and InMemoryEventStore.loadSnapshot returns null unconditionally (line 51). Every direct test caller uses the default fromSequence: 0, which the '<= 1' branch happens to get right. The bug bites the day someone adds snapshot support to the helper - at which point a snapshot's own last event replays twice, which is exactly the kind of double-apply that is hard to diagnose.

The helper is used by ~103 test sites with 8 subclasses, so getting it right matters for everything built on it later.

One-line fix, one two-line unit test (getEvents(pid, fromSequence: 1) should skip event 1). No migration. Zero production blast radius - tests only.

Genuine cleanup: bundle into any sweep.

title: TransactionImportedEvent.blockHeight is non-nullable, so an unproven import records the genesis block
description:
Found 2026-09-18 while aligning the last sites for V-79; I tried to fix it there and backed the change out because it needs a wider edit than that bead's scope.

TransactionImportedEvent.blockHeight is a non-nullable int, and its fromMap casts 'blockHeight' as int. SPVActor._buildTransactionData therefore has to emit 'blockHeight': blockHeight ?? 0 (spv_actor.dart:2426, and a literal 0 on its error path), and WalletManagerActor reads it back with '?? 0'. So a transaction imported with no BUMP records height 0 - the genesis block - rather than an absence.

This is the same defect V-79 fixed one level down for UTXOs, still present for TRANSACTIONS. It is currently harmless because the height only reaches a UTXO row when hasMerkleProof is true (wallet_manager_actor.dart ~600, 'blockHeight: hasMerkleProof ? blockHeight : null'), so the guard keeps the 0 off UTXO rows. But it is latent: the rule holds by a guard at a distance rather than because an absence is representable, and per V-79 the transaction row's height is now the confirmed test for transactions too.

Under the library's own principle (spv-understanding.md, 'What this library is for'): where evidence is missing the honest record is an absence, not a plausible value.

Scope: make TransactionImportedEvent.blockHeight nullable (event, fromMap, getWalletEventData), drop the two '?? 0' in spv_actor.dart and the one in wallet_manager_actor.dart, and check the projection's transaction-row write and BitcoinTransaction.isConfirmed still behave. No journals to preserve (pre-release). Attempted naively it fails with 'type Null is not a subtype of type int in type cast' in test/services/received_ancestor_retention_test.dart:111, which builds the event straight from the map - that test needs updating too.

Test: an import with no BUMP records no height, and does not report as confirmed.
close_reason: Fixed as V-80: TransactionImportedEvent.blockHeight and RecordImportedTransactionCommand.blockHeight are nullable, both ?? 0 in SPVActor and the two in WalletManagerActor are gone, and the aggregate writes no blockHeight key when nothing proves one. Tests: test/actors/unproven_import_has_no_height_test.dart, test/core/imported_transaction_height_test.dart (10). Five fix sites each re-broken on main and the covering test confirmed failing.

title: Address junctions cover only imported transactions, and their input links are invented
description:
Found by the libspiffy-1kd5 reachability sweep; see doc/reachability-sweep-2026-09-18.md section 4, D-3.

Two defects in the transaction-address junction table that backs getTransactionAddresses (a public read-model API with no lib/ consumer; it exists for applications).

(a) ONE OF N ROUTES. _createTransactionAddressJunctions has exactly one caller: _handleTransactionImported. TransactionRecordedEvent, our own outgoing transactions, never builds junctions, so an address-centric query is blind to everything the wallet sent. This is the same one-of-N-routes pattern V-81 hit on the channel closing txid.

(b) FABRICATED INPUT LINKS, wallet_projection.dart:1607-1617.
  - amount: BigInt.zero, // Would need parent tx to get exact amount
    The parent amounts ARE available: the import event carries its BEEF ancestors and _storeAncestors runs a few lines earlier on the same event.
  - the loop pairs sendingAddresses[i] with parsedTx.inputs[i] positionally. sendingAddresses is a derived list of addresses, not a per-input list, so the vin index on each link is unfounded whenever the two do not correspond.

FIX: build junctions on the outgoing route too; take input amounts from the stored ancestors and key each link to the input it actually belongs to (outpoint), not to a list position. Where a parent is genuinely unavailable, record an absence rather than zero.

TEST: (a) record an outgoing transaction and assert getTransactionAddresses returns its links; empty on the code as found. (b) import a transaction whose sendingAddresses count differs from its input count and assert the vin/amount on each link; wrong on the code as found.

title: WalletTransactionSigner signs a foreign-key P2PK input instead of refusing it
description:
Reported by the libspiffy-kfvv lane (V-93), and rated by that lane as the real remaining defect in this area.

WalletTransactionSigner.unlockFor (lib/src/core/wallet/transaction_signer.dart, around line 212) returns SignatureOnlyUnlockBuilder for a P2PK input UNCONDITIONALLY, while the P2PKH branch a few lines below it checks that the wallet holds the key (requireKeyForP2pkh). So a P2PK input locked to a key the wallet does not hold is signed with whatever key the attributed address names, and produces a silently invalid unlocking script rather than a clear error.

V-93 keeps such an output out of every SELECTION, so nothing reaches the signer on its own. What remains is a caller naming the outpoint explicitly - SignTransactionCommand over a chosen input. That is a guard, not a selection rule, which is why V-93 did not cover it.

FIX: give the P2PK branch the same key check the P2PKH branch has, and fail with the same shape of error. A signature that cannot satisfy the script should be refused where it is built, not discovered when a node rejects the transaction.

TEST: SignTransactionCommand over a P2PK input locked to a foreign key is refused, naming the reason; one locked to a wallet key still signs.

title: eventador ProjectionActor has no way to cancel an event awaiter
description:
Found 2026-09-18 by the libspiffy-kyw lane (V-82).

IMPLEMENTED UPSTREAM AND NOW CONSUMED LOCALLY. NOT RELEASED.

eventador commit 36b30cf on main in ../eventador (local only, not pushed, not published):
- AwaitEventApplied gains an optional awaitId, the caller's own name for the registration, matched by value.
- CancelEventAwait(awaitId) drops every registration carrying it, cancels their timers, and answers each one AwaitFailed(reason: 'cancelled'), so a caller waiting on the original ask is released immediately rather than at the timeout.
- Answered with EventAwaitCancelled(cancelled: n). Cancelling an unregistered id is not an error.
- Additive and backwards compatible: a registration with no awaitId behaves exactly as before and no cancel can touch it.
- Four tests, three mutations each caught. CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased; version deliberately left at 3.0.0 so the bump goes with the release. Full eventador suite 276 passing.

libspiffy consumes it as of V-84 (commit 0433678) through a dependency_overrides stanza in pubspec.yaml pointing at ../eventador. libspiffy-kyw (c) is closed on the strength of it.

THIS BEAD NOW TRACKS ONE THING: the release. Until it happens,
- a clone of libspiffy on its own does not resolve (it needs the sibling checkout),
- libspiffy cannot be published (dart pub publish refuses a package with dependency_overrides - which is also why this cannot ship by accident).

To close it: publish eventador (3.1.0 by semver - additive), bump libspiffy's constraint from ^3.0.0 to ^3.1.0, and DELETE the dependency_overrides stanza from pubspec.yaml (it is commented with this bead id). Then re-run the suite.

title: Benford split reports outcomes it cannot evidence: a total failure answers success:true, and transactionCount is inflated by targetUtxoCount
description:
Split out of libspiffy-el95 (items 4 and 5) by the 19 Sep triage. Filed as ONE bead because they are the same defect class in the same files with the same test harness: the reply states a number or an outcome the code cannot evidence.

(A) A SPLIT THAT FAILS EARLY VANISHES SILENTLY. benford_coordinator_actor.dart:156-166:
  final attempt = await _splitSingleUtxo(...);
  if (attempt == null) continue;
_splitSingleUtxo returns null on FOUR paths, none producing an outcome: :300 source UTXO too small for targetCount + estimatedFee; :308 reservation refused; :338 build or SIGN failure; :409 any exception ('Failed to build or record Benford split transaction').

_replyIfSettled (:265-282) builds the reply purely from pending.outcomes. If EVERY source UTXO fails early, outcomes is empty, so failed is empty, so the caller gets:
  SplitUTXOsResponse(success: true, error: null, splitCount: 0, txids: [], splits: [])
A TOTAL FAILURE IS REPORTED AS A SUCCESS. Partial failures vanish the same way - splits.length < utxosToSplit.length with nothing saying which sources were skipped or why. The reasons are logged and discarded.

The type system already supports honesty: :392-398 returns a _SplitAttempt carrying notRecorded: SplitTransactionOutcome(status: notRecorded, error: ...). The four early paths just do not use it. SplitTransactionStatus has no member for 'not built'; adding one costs nothing journal-wise because it is a MESSAGE enum in coordinator_messages.dart, not a journaled event type.

(B) transactionCount IS NUMERICALLY WRONG. wallet_coordinator_actor.dart:1962-1973:
  transactionCount: response.splitCount ?? 0,
  newUtxoCount: response.splitCount ?? 0,
  totalFeePaid: BigInt.zero,
splitCount is a UTXO count, not a transaction count - benford_coordinator_actor.dart:277 computes made.length * pending.command.targetUtxoCount, and wallet_messages.dart:287 says '// Number of UTXOs created'. So newUtxoCount is right and transactionCount is INFLATED BY targetUtxoCount. With the default targetUtxoCount: 5, one split transaction is reported to the host as five. The honest value is right there: response.txids.length.

(C) totalFeePaid: BigInt.zero IS A MANUFACTURED VALUE. The fee is genuinely unavailable at that point - SplitUTXOsResponse has no fee field and SplitTransactionOutcome carries only txid, sourceUtxoKey, status, networkStatus, error. The fee is computed and discarded inside _splitSingleUtxo (estimatedFee). So zero is not a measurement, it is an invention - exactly what spv-understanding.md forbids. Fix by plumbing a fee through, or by making the field nullable so 'unknown' is expressible rather than stated as zero. An absence is honest; zero is not.

Ready-made harness: test/actors/benford_split_broadcast_outcome_test.dart:339-375 already builds a scripted SplitUTXOsResponse with splitCount: 3 and reads the emitted UTXOSplitCompleteEvent. A failing assertion drops straight in. The killer fail-first test for (A) is 'all sources too small -> success: true'.

Raised from P4 to P2: false success on a signing failure, plus a demonstrably wrong integer and a fabricated zero on a public API event.
close_reason: Fixed as V-108. q28i: every source that builds no transaction is now reported (SplitTransactionStatus.notBuilt, nullable txid) so a total failure is no longer a success; transactionCount is txids.length rather than the UTXO count; totalFeePaid is summed from a real SplitTransactionOutcome.feePaid. y0ce: the 10 us per-address sleep removed, the loop index already makes the command id unique. Also fixed in the same seam: withFeePerKb was given satoshis per byte.

title: A plugin-managed UTXO can fund a payment channel, spending a token or earmarked output as plain funds
description:
Found 2026-09-18 by the libspiffy-8egy lane (V-83) while reworking funding candidate selection.

ChannelFunding.fundingCandidates builds its own spendability predicate (isAvailable, !isSpent, !isReserved, no deferred holder, not watch-only, and now unlockable-alone). It does NOT exclude plugin-managed UTXOs, which WalletBalances.isSpendable does exclude everywhere else.

So a UTXO a plugin manages - a token output, a funding earmark - can be selected as ordinary funding for a channel and spent as plain satoshis. For a tokenised output that destroys the token: the output is consumed and the plugin's state no longer has an output behind it.

Pre-existing, not introduced by V-83 (the lane left it alone as out of scope, correctly).

Fix: have fundingCandidates go through the same plugin-managed exclusion the rest of the wallet uses (WalletBalances.isSpendable, or whatever part of it applies), rather than a second hand-rolled predicate. Check the other hand-rolled predicates for the same gap while there.

Test: a wallet holding a plugin-managed UTXO and no other funds cannot fund a channel, and says why.
close_reason: Fixed as V-85 (commit 0db7782). fundingCandidates now selects with WalletBalances.isSpendable and narrows it with the two conditions funding adds (no deferred holder, unlockable alone), instead of a hand-rolled predicate that omitted plugin-managed outputs. Tests in test/core/wallet/wallet_collaborators_test.dart, re-broken on main and confirmed failing.

title: pgt remainder: Map and List<Event> replies, and replies without success/error
description: From libspiffy-pgt (partial, commit after b95280d). Remaining: WalletManagerActor Map replies {'error','walletId'} (not found, load failure; pinned by wallet_manager_actor_test:97) and catch-all {'error','type':'wallet_manager_error'}, consumed by Map-aware receivers in AggregateSigningClient, channel manager, payment coordinator (V-31 refusal receiver), Benford and invoice coordinators: move together to typed ActorResponse failures. Replies without success/error still bare Message: SPVValidationResult, BEEFValidationResult x2, TransactionValidationResult, InvoiceDetailsResponse, InvoiceStatusMessage, InvoicesListMessage, BroadcastSuccess/FailedMessage, TransactionStatusMessage, FeeQuoteMessage (wraps error Map), FeeEstimateMessage, SPVErrorMessage, SPVStatusMessage, HeaderSyncStatusMessage, BlockHeadersProcessedMessage, WalletListMessage, ImportCancelResponse/ImportProgressMessage. Triaged 19 Sep and split into two beads. The survey confirmed this is NOT a cleanup item: 49 distinct test files, ~61 send sites and 42 receive sites across three clusters.

THE KEY STRUCTURAL FINDING: clusters A and B ARE NOT SEPARABLE. Six receivers (aggregate_signing_client.dart:522, payment_coordinator_actor.dart:1580/:1601, benford_coordinator_actor.dart:702/:729, payment_channel_manager_actor.dart:3023) discriminate on 'payload is Map' alone and cannot tell the WalletManagerActor map from the BitcoinWalletAggregate map. Converting one producer leaves the is-Map branch live for the other and the receiver's own comment lying. So A+B is one bead, sequenced internally A then B1 then B2.

Cluster C IS separable and parallel-safe: extends-ActorResponse is source-compatible for receivers because dactor extracts payload and payload returns this - the transformation the bareReplies group already proved. Its only cost is breadth.

THINGS THE BEAD DID NOT KNOW, now recorded on the children:
- A GAP: wallet_coordinator_actor.dart tells the wallet manager with itself as sender at six sites and its dispatch chain (:319-345) has NO is-Map branch, so an error map is SILENTLY DROPPED; its four ask<XResponse> sites would take a cast failure on the same map.
- B1's blast radius is bigger than it looks: the typed chain covers 13 commands while wallet_commands.dart declares 35, so ~22 command types land in the fallback.
- B2's raw List<Event> IS LOAD-BEARING and must not collapse to success/error: all 18 _askAggregate sites feed it to _broadcastEvents, which forwards typed ChannelEvents to the external P2P broadcaster, and :485 reads lockTimeUnix off a specific event with a comment saying recomputing it locally would be wrong. Four test files unwrap events from it.
- TWO OF THE 18 CLUSTER-C TYPES ARE DEAD (spv_messages.dart:212 TransactionValidationResult and :274 BEEFValidationResult, the latter explicitly hidden by spv_actor.dart:15) - delete rather than convert. Ten of the remaining sixteen have zero lib receivers.
- TWO CLUSTER-C TYPES ENCODE FAILURE DISHONESTLY and need more than a base class: FeeQuoteMessage's only field is a Map and three of its four send sites put {'error':...} inside it; FeeEstimateMessage signals failure as BigInt.zero, a plausible-looking value where the honest record is an absence.
- The repo already defines 'done' for this work: actor_response_base_test.dart loops over actor_reply_shape_characterization_test.dart's replies + bareReplies maps. Converted types move from bareReplies into replies.
- Both aggregates and the channel manager are exported via internals.dart, and most cluster-C types via libspiffy.dart:48. WalletManagerActor's Map replies are de-facto public with no compiler-visible symbol, so a consumer doing 'is Map' breaks SILENTLY rather than at compile time.

Split out:
- P3: untyped failure replies - WalletManagerActor Maps and both aggregates (clusters A+B, one lane, sequenced A -> B1 -> B2, B2 riskiest)
- P3: sixteen reply messages onto ActorResponse, two dead ones deleted (cluster C, parallel-safe)

title: Script builders with an empty parse() override silently rebuild wrong scripts
description:
Found by the libspiffy-1kd5 reachability sweep; see doc/reachability-sweep-2026-09-18.md section 6.

Four script builders override parse(SVScript) with an empty body:
  services/transaction/builder/partial_witness_unlock_builder.dart:32
  services/transaction/builder/pp2_lock_builder.dart:34
  services/transaction/builder/pp2_unlock_builder.dart:22
  services/transaction/builder/hodl_lockbuilder.dart:27 carries a TODO above code that does parse.
And pp1_lock_builder.dart:52 has a TODO for issuance identity anchor signature validation.

dartsv calls parse when a builder is constructed from an existing script. An empty override leaves every field at its default, so any script rebuilt from a parsed one is silently wrong rather than failing. If these builders are only ever constructed from parameters and never from a script, the honest form is to throw UnimplementedError from parse rather than to accept the call and do nothing.

title: Exported ReadModelStorage defaults an unspecified network to mainnet while NetworkName defaults to testnet
description:
Split out of libspiffy-3gd (item 6) by the 19 Sep triage. Premise confirmed; the honest framing is narrower than the bead title.

Two defaults disagree:
- NetworkName.canonical (utils/network_name.dart:42-46) returns 'testnet' for null.
- All three storage backends return 'mainnet' for null: in_memory_wallet_storage.dart:180, isar_wallet_storage.dart:105, postgres_wallet_storage.dart:100 (COALESCE(@network, 'mainnet')).
- Two model defaults side with storage: wallet_state.dart:140 and wallet_read_model.dart:58 both default 'mainnet' in empty().
- A THIRD spelling exists at the actor layer: 'test' (libspiffy_actor_system.dart:90,225, import_actor.dart:1108, coordinator_messages.dart:93).

The 'mainnet' default is currently DEAD IN-TREE. Every path libspiffy itself takes canonicalises first: WalletProjection._handleWalletCreated passes NetworkName.canonical(...) (wallet_projection.dart:232), and the aggregate agrees (wallet_keys.dart:128, wallet_lifecycle.dart:98). The other three storeWallet calls pass the row's existing network.

So this is not a live bug - it is a TRAP IN EXPORTED API SURFACE. ReadModelStorage is exported from lib/libspiffy.dart:22. An external consumer calling storeWallet(id, name) with no networkType writes 'mainnet'; every later reader then gets NetworkName.isMainnet('mainnet') == true and dartsv.NetworkType.MAIN address encoding, on a wallet the aggregate considers testnet. That is exactly the V-1/V-2 failure mode - mainnet/testnet disagreement between layers - waiting in the public API.

The fix needs a DECISION, not just an edit: route the default through NetworkName.canonical (so null means testnet, consistent everywhere), or make networkType required (a breaking API change that removes the ambiguity entirely). Also reconcile the actor layer's third spelling ('test').

Fail-first test is easy and belongs in the cross-backend contract so all three agree: storeWallet(id, name) with no network, assert the stored network.

No migration needed for the default change itself, but if any rows were written 'mainnet' by the old default they would need auditing - check before assuming none exist.

ENTANGLED with the single-outpoint-lookup bead: same three backends, same read_model_storage.dart, both want a contract test. Do this one FIRST - it is small and decision-led.
close_reason:
Fixed on main (audit V-113). All three ReadModelStorage backends now create a wallet row with WalletRowRules.defaultNetwork = NetworkName.canonical(null) = testnet, and canonicalise any supplied spelling, so the actor/P2P vocabulary ('main'/'test'/'regtest') cannot sit in a row beside the read model's own. WalletState.empty and WalletReadModel.empty default to NetworkName.canonical(null) too.

The decision the bead asked for was answered by the interface's own contract: a null networkType already MEANS 'keep the stored network', as it does for rootAddress and metadata, so making it required would contradict the merge rule V-106 made uniform. Canonical-everywhere, not required. Testnet is also the safe direction to be wrong in.

Audited rather than assumed: libspiffy's only INSERT path (WalletProjection._handleWalletCreated) has always passed NetworkName.canonical(...), and its other three storeWallet calls are updates that resupply the row's network and bail with no row. No row libspiffy wrote ever took the old default; nothing to migrate, and no row is rewritten.

Third spelling reconciled, not renamed: 'test' is the dartsv/P2P vocabulary, not a fourth network. What has to hold is that it resolves to the same network, now pinned by a test that reads each layer's declared default.

Tests: the fail-first test is in the SHARED test/storage/wallet_lifecycle_contract.dart so all three backends run it, plus three in test/utils/network_name_test.dart pinning cross-layer agreement. Nine mutations, each failing alone. Three existing tests re-aimed (contract re-create test, wallet_state_test, bn03 copy fixture) - all had restated the old default.

title: No Isar old-store test for DeferredPaymentEntity.competingTxids
description:
Split out of libspiffy-el95 (item 2) by the 19 Sep triage. Premise true, risk near-zero, and a legitimate close-as-wont-do candidate - recorded here so the decision is deliberate rather than forgotten.

No test opens an Isar store written before competingTxids existed. The field is covered by test/storage/deferred_payment_contract.dart:258-272 and postgres_deferred_payment_test.dart:143-145, but every one writes a FRESH row with the current schema. The untested claim is the entity doc at libspiffy_schemas.dart:402-404: 'empty for a row stored before the property existed.'

WHY THE RISK IS NEAR-ZERO: the generated reader already guarantees it. libspiffy_schemas.g.dart:7069 -
  object.competingTxids = reader.readStringList(offsets[1]) ?? [];
An old row has no bytes at that offset, so it reads []. The claim is true by construction.

WHY THE FIXTURE IS EXPENSIVE: the three existing Isar migration tests (isar_index_migration_test.dart:116, 165, 200) are INDEX-ONLY. _withIndexes (:25-44) clones a generated CollectionSchema and swaps only its indexes map, reusing the generated serialize/deserialize/estimateSize. A PROPERTY removal cannot reuse those closures - they write and read by offsets[n] derived from the property map, so a shortened properties map needs a hand-written serialize and estimateSize for the former entity. There is no precedent in this repo for a property-level old-schema fixture.

So: non-trivial fixture cost to test Isar's own documented behaviour. Either close this as wont-do with the generated-reader line above as the justification, or do it properly IF a property-level fixture is ever needed for something else - at which point this becomes a cheap second case rather than the reason to build the machinery.

title: Wave 3 lane 1 follow-ups: non-concurrency persist errors escape as raw ServerException; currentPersistenceIds unbounded SELECT DISTINCT; no SecurityContext for verify-full with a private CA
close_reason:
Fixed as V-105 (commit d8a6a6c). All three items.

(1) Non-concurrency persist errors escaped raw. _append turned a 23505 on uk_persistence_sequence into ConcurrencyException and rethrew everything else, so a duplicate event_id, an over-long value or a permission error reached the caller as the driver's own exception naming no journal. Every non-concurrency failure is now an EventStoreException naming the persistence id, the batch size and the SQLSTATE, with the original as cause and raised via Error.throwWithStackTrace so the ORIGINAL stack survives. Concurrency detection untouched and still the only thing reported as a conflict.

(2) currentPersistenceIds was SELECT DISTINCT over a journal that only grows (EXPLAIN confirmed Seq Scan into HashAggregate reading every row). Now a keyset skip-scan over the EXISTING v001 index, paged, so work follows the number of distinct ids rather than journal length. The cost was fixed, never the content: no migration, nothing stored differently, no row trimmed. Per the protocol the tests OBSERVE cost rather than timing it - they capture the store's real SQL through a visibleForTesting hook, run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON), walk the plan tree summing actual rows x loops over every scan node on event_envelopes, assert every access is an Index Only Scan on idx_event_envelopes_persistence_id, and count round trips with a small page size.

CONTRACT CHANGE: the read is paged rather than one snapshot, so it no longer matches the Akka currentPersistenceIds semantics the eventador interface doc cites. Documented on the method. I verified there is NO caller in lib/ - only tests and test fakes - so nothing in libspiffy is affected today.

(3) PostgresConfig gains sslRootCertPath, sslRootCertBytes and securityContext, all optional and defaulting to null, so a server behind a private CA can be verified. Defaults are byte-for-byte unchanged. A CA with no explicit sslMode selects verifyFull rather than require, because under require the driver ignores certificate problems and the CA would be decorative; an explicit mode always wins, and copyWith applies the same rule so the trap cannot be reintroduced by copying. A CA that cannot be read or parsed throws ArgumentError rather than connecting with an empty trust store.

ITEM 3 IS HONESTLY PARTIAL: the tests prove the CA reaches ConnectionSettings.securityContext / PoolSettings.securityContext, NOT that a TLS handshake against a private-CA server succeeds or that a certificate from another CA is rejected. No TLS server was stood up and no such claim is made.

No migration needed or written; the skip scan uses the existing v001 index. Postgres 187/187 (178 baseline plus 9 new). Three mutations verified independently on main.

title: Client-side _handleRecordPayment lacks the non-negative and sum-to-funding invariants the server half has

title: Fail a reclaim immediately when its inputs were spent by another transaction, instead of waiting for an ARC poll
description:
Follow-up from the libspiffy-87a lane (V-69).

If the recipient's copy of a deferred payment reaches the network first, our reclaim's self-spend is the one rejected - first seen wins, there is no replace-by-fee on this network and no fee that changes the outcome (spv-understanding.md Critical Implementation Note 3). When that happens the reclaim's own deferred record is left outstanding until ARC reports it REJECTED and the normal failure path resolves it. That is correct but slow: the wallet already learns the inputs were spent by another transaction (applyInputSpent), so the reclaim could be failed at that moment rather than waiting for a poll.

Scope: when an input held by a reclaim's self-spend is observed spent by a transaction that is not the self-spend, resolve the reclaim as failed and say why. Do not touch the fee, and do not add retry-at-a-higher-fee logic of any kind - if the counterparty's transaction was seen first, there is no recovery, only an accurate state.

Test: an outstanding payment is reclaimed, the recipient's copy is seen on the network first, and the reclaim resolves as failed without an ARC poll.

title: Decide whether an input with a known address but no parent should be linked without an amount
description:
Follow-up from V-89 (libspiffy-o9h6), reported by the lane and deliberately left out of scope because migration v023 belonged to another lane.

An input whose address we know from the event's sendingAddresses but whose parent transaction we no longer hold - chiefly a replay of journals written before TransactionImportedEvent carried its ancestors - is currently left UNLINKED. That is honest (better than the old fabricated zero on a positional vin) but it is not the fullest honest answer: we do know the address was on the input side, we just do not know the amount.

TransactionAddressLink.amount is non-nullable BigInt and the Postgres column is transaction_addresses.amount BIGINT NOT NULL (v001_initial_schema.dart:260); the Isar TransactionAddressEntity.amount is `late String`. Recording "this address was on the input side, amount unknown" needs amount to become BigInt? plus an Isar schema regen and a Postgres migration dropping the NOT NULL.

PUBLIC API: TransactionAddressLink and TransactionAddresses are exported models, so amount becoming nullable is a breaking change for readers. Follow the V-80 and V-88 precedent: an absence rather than a plausible value.

DECIDE FIRST whether the case is common enough to be worth the migration: it only arises on a replay of pre-ancestors journals and on imports whose BEEF we no longer hold. If it is rare, leaving those inputs unlinked may be the right permanent answer - in which case close this with that reasoning recorded rather than doing the work.

title: Postgres journal ids are assigned at insert, so concurrent writers can commit out of id order and id-keyed replay/live streams can skip a late-committing event
description: From wave 3 lane 1 (S-09/S-10). Writers on different persistence ids get ids at INSERT time but may commit in a different order; a replay or live stream that advances by id (id > @lastId) can pass a lower id that commits later and never deliver it. Planned fix: one journal-wide advisory lock so ids commit in order, plus ordered publishing (hold back publication until earlier appends are published). Tests: park one writer after INSERT before COMMIT, and one after COMMIT before publish.

title: Inbound channel protocol messages other than channel_open are not idempotent; a duplicate is answered with a rejection and sometimes channel_error
description:
Found 2026-09-19 by the libspiffy-1n3 lane (V-100).

V-100 made the server's inbound channel_open idempotent for a repeat naming the same funding output: the repeat is a no-op answered success, rather than a rejection that routes to _reportFailure(tellPeer: true) and tells the client its channel failed. That fix was needed to make ResendChannelOpenCommand actually work - otherwise the repair is answered by the very message that says the channel was abandoned.

The other inbound protocol messages have no such treatment. channel_accept, refund_signed and payment_ack all forward to the aggregate, which refuses a duplicate on a state guard, and in some paths that refusal reaches the peer as channel_error. So a counterparty that re-sends any of those - for exactly the reason V-100 exists, because it is not sure the first one arrived - gets told the channel failed.

This is the same shape of defect as V-100, on three more messages. Worth a deliberate pass rather than fixing them one at a time when each is next touched.

For each of channel_accept, refund_signed and payment_ack, decide what a repeat NAMING THE SAME FACT means (it is a repeat, journal nothing, answer success) versus a repeat naming a DIFFERENT fact (that is not a repeat and must still be refused) - that is the distinction V-100 drew for channel_open, and it is the one that keeps the guard narrow.

Note this is the peer-facing half of the same question V-100 answered for the host-facing half. There is no public re-send command for these three either; whether they need one is a separate question from whether a duplicate is handled honestly.

Test: for each message type, send it twice identically and assert nothing is journaled the second time, success is answered, and no channel_error reaches the peer; then send a conflicting second one and assert it is still refused.
close_reason: Fixed as V-110 (payment-channel seam, pass 2). fg06: AcknowledgePaymentMessage carries sender: _replyTo, the adapter's handlePaymentAcknowledged sends channel_error on refusal, and the coordinator routes the response. y8x3: channel_accept and refund_signed now tell a repeat naming the same fact from one naming a different fact; payment_ack already had its guard. Also fixed: _askAggregate treated an empty event list as a failure, which broke every idempotent path including two that already existed.

title: Proof status follow-ups: rebuilt orphaned proof row loses its block hash (revert event has it, markMerkleProofOrphaned does not record it); SPVActor could re-check pendingHeader proofs at startup

title: RecordImportedTransactionCommand has no isRecorded guard, unlike recordOutgoing
description:
Found 2026-09-18 by the libspiffy-f5p2 lane (V-86).

PaymentChannelManagerActor guards its wallet writes with a read-model check (_walletHoldsTransaction), which is a no-op when the manager is built without a storage argument (tests, degraded configurations). In that configuration a resumed close could journal a second TransactionImportedEvent for the same transaction - the same row, no corruption, but a duplicate event in the journal.

The wallet aggregate already has the general answer for the outgoing side: recordOutgoing checks whether the transaction is recorded before emitting. RecordImportedTransactionCommand has no equivalent.

Fix: give the imported path the same guard in the aggregate, so idempotency does not depend on every caller checking a read model first. Cheap and general - it protects every sender, not just the channel manager.

Test: the same RecordImportedTransactionCommand handled twice journals one TransactionImportedEvent.
close_reason: Fixed on main as V-92

title: BenfordCoordinator: broadcasts before recording the split, spends the source immediately instead of deferring, reads the wallet type from the read model (refuses a split right after wallet-manager create)
description: From libspiffy-hhj (lane T) triage of benford_split_test. Record-before-broadcast ordering, deferred spend consistent with payments (V-16 applies it on SEEN_ON_NETWORK), and wait for / consult the aggregate rather than the read model for wallet type.
close_reason: Fixed with mutation-verified tests; report section 11 V-44 to V-51

title: PaymentChannelManagerActor has no reply guarantee: a handler whose own catch escapes leaves its caller waiting forever
description:
Found 2026-09-19 by the libspiffy-q7a lane while removing _sendErrorResponse (V-104).

All twenty request-shaped handlers in PaymentChannelManagerActor answer their own failures: each wraps its body in try/catch and replies in the matching response type to a sender captured before its first await. That is the right pattern and it is used consistently.

What is gone, deliberately, is the top-level net. The old outer catch called a _sendErrorResponse that knew only two of the twenty message types and replied to context.sender - which after a handler's awaits is the sender of whatever message arrived NEXT. So for two types it duplicated a reply already sent, and for the rest it did nothing; either way it could answer the wrong actor. Extending it to twenty arms would have propagated the wrong-sender bug eighteen times, so it was removed and the outer catch now logs at severe.

The residual gap: if a handler's own catch ever escapes - a throw in the catch block itself, or a path that returns before replying - its caller waits on a reply that never comes, until the ask times out, with only a log to say why.

The right shape is a per-handler GUARANTEE, not a type-guessing generic: capture the sender once in onMessage, and assert (in debug, or via a wrapper that each handler returns its response through) that a reply was sent before the handler returned. That makes 'every request is answered' a checkable property rather than a convention twenty methods happen to follow.

This is a design bead, not cleanup. It is also a good candidate for a test that mutates one handler to swallow its own error and asserts the caller still gets an answer.

Related: libspiffy-ro84 is moving actor replies onto typed ActorResponse failures generally; if that lands first, this should be built on top of it rather than beside it.
close_reason: Decided and shipped as V-111. m0xj: 'required' was tried empirically and does not fit yet (an empty read model is not behaviour-neutral; blocked on the fixture work in libspiffy-tg4d), so the other branch was done properly - the storage parameter documents each of the four guarantees that degrade, preStart warns when it is absent so the configuration is never silent, and _walletHoldsTransaction states that false means 'not known to'. yypk: 'every request is answered' is now a checkable property - every request type is driven into a failure and must answer in its own response type, with a coverage guard that reads onMessage's dispatch out of the source.

title: A client never holds the cooperative settlement: the server's countersignature is received and dropped
description:
Found 2026-09-18 by the libspiffy-f5p2 lane (V-86), which fixed the settlement recording and could not close this half.

_handleAcknowledgePayment is the SERVER path: the server combines both signatures and holds the fully signed settlement, so a server-side close records it (V-86). The server's countersignature does come back to the client in PaymentAcknowledgedResponse, but channel_p2p_adapter._handlePaymentAck (~line 466) only LOGS it. Nothing journals it, so the client's latestPaymentTxHex stays the UNSIGNED template.

An unsigned template's txid is not the txid the signed transaction will have, so recording it would create a wallet UTXO at an outpoint that can never exist. V-86 therefore records nothing on a client cooperative close and leaves the channel in 'closing' - the honest state, but it means a client's cooperative return leg never reaches its wallet. Today that leg is covered only by the expiry/refund route.

Note the reply: _handleCloseChannel answers ChannelClosedResponse(success: true) even when nothing was finalised and the channel stays 'closing'. Decide whether that reply should distinguish the two, or whether the caller is expected to query the state.

Scope: a command and event for 'the client journals the server's countersignature', plus a hunk in channel_p2p_adapter._handlePaymentAck to send it. Then the client's close records its share exactly as the server's does - the V-86 helpers (_returnLeg / _recordReturnLegInWallet) are already shared and need nothing new.

Test: client and server open a channel, pay, close cooperatively; BOTH wallets show the settlement in history with their own share as a pending UTXO.
close_reason: Fixed on main as V-90

title: Channel funding failure leaves wallet inputs reserved forever; nothing ever releases them
description:
Found 2026-09-19 by the survey for libspiffy-1n3 (round 2b).

grep finds NO ReleaseUTXO of any kind in payment_channel_manager_actor.dart. The funding path records the funding transaction with deferSpend: true (payment_channel_manager_actor.dart ~1572: 'the inputs stay reserved by this transaction until ARC accepts it') and only calls _spendFundingInputs (~1460) after a successful ARC reply. That is correct: on a recorded failure the inputs are RESERVED, not spent, which is what makes retrying the same funding transaction safe.

The gap is that nothing ever ends the reservation. A channel abandoned after a funding broadcast failure holds its inputs out of the spendable balance permanently. There is no expiry on the reservation and no command that drops it.

DO NOT fix this by releasing the inputs when the broadcast fails. BSV is first-seen-wins with no replace-by-fee: a broadcast whose reply was lost may well have reached the mempool, and releasing its inputs so they can be spent elsewhere would produce a conflicting transaction that loses the race and strands the funds. The library cannot know which happened.

The honest shape is app-driven, matching 'the library records, the app decides': a public command that abandons a channel whose funding never landed and releases its reservation, which the app issues once IT has decided the funding is dead. The library should make the state legible (the reservation, the failure, the attempt count) and let the app call it.

Relation to libspiffy-1n3: 1n3 adds the public retry-funding command. This is its counterpart - the give-up path - and the two together are what make a failed funding recoverable in either direction. Worth doing in the same lane if the lane has room, otherwise straight after.

Test: fund a channel with a broadcast that fails, assert the inputs are still reserved and the balance reflects that; issue the abandon command; assert the inputs are selectable again and nothing was marked spent.
close_reason:
Fixed as V-102 (commit faaabdd) - but THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG, and the correction is the finding. Third time in this backlog (with p6ot and kfvv).

The bead said 'nothing ever releases them'. Half right. The funding inputs are held twice: an ordinary reservation at build time (channel_funding.dart:265-280, 1h expiry, priority 10) and a DEFERRED HOLD written when the funding is recorded with deferSpend: true (deferred_payments.dart:515-526), which has NO expiry, priority 1<<30, and is explicitly skipped by ReleaseUTXOsCommand (utxo_reservations.dart:72-74), thrown on by the singular ReleaseUTXOCommand (:176-180), and passed over by cleanupExpired (:267-269). So the generic release path genuinely cannot touch it.

But the funding is registered as a deferred payment with purpose 'channel-funding' (payment_channel_manager_actor.dart:1805), and the existing public CancelDeferredPaymentCommand releases holds. It ALSO already implements the constraint I wrote into this bead as though it needed building: ARC is asked for live network status first (wallet_coordinator_actor.dart:1134-1149), force bypasses only 'ARC was unreachable' and never 'ARC knows it', the aggregate re-checks at journaling time (deferred_payments.dart:298-302), and _markSeen takes a cancelled payment back to seen if the transaction surfaces later. The money was recoverable all along; the test proving it passes on untouched lib/.

THE REAL DEFECT WAS CREATED BY V-100 THE DAY BEFORE. RetryChannelFundingCommand gates only on the channel's status, and a failed funding leaves the channel in refundSigned permanently because _applyFundingBroadcastFailed never touches status. So after an app cancelled to get its money back, the channel still looked retryable and a retry re-broadcast a funding transaction whose inputs had been released and may since have been spent elsewhere.

_fundingHoldReleased now reads the wallet's deferred-payment record - not the UTXO rows, because an 'available' UTXO says only that nothing holds it NOW, equally true of an input another payment has since taken; the payment record says who released it and why, which is what a refusal must be able to state. Placed in _fundClientChannel rather than the retry handler so one rule covers the public retry, the internal OpenChannelMessage and the restart-resume path alike. The DeferredPaymentState switch is exhaustive so a state added later must be classified rather than falling into a silent 'still held', and an ABSENT RECORD NEVER REFUSES - a funding recorded before holds were journaled is an absence, not evidence.

Deliberately NOT done, with the argument: no new ChannelStatus and no abandon command. ExpireChannelCommand already gives a refundSigned channel a terminal route once past lockTime; before that, refundSigned IS the truth (the refund is countersigned, the funding was never broadcast), and an 'abandoned' status would assert an app intention the library does not know. Both facts are already legible: PaymentChannel.errorMessage for 'this funding failed', and the deferred payment with purpose 'channel-funding' + heldInputs + recipientAddresses ['channel:<id>'] for 'the money is recoverable'.

No public API change, no new event type, no migration. 7 tests; three mutations verified on main including the absence rule inverted. A test fake was corrected rather than an assertion adjusted: _RecordingArc threw without a status code so ArcException.isNotFound was false; real ARC answers 404.

Filed separately: a wallet frozen by a journaled hold reports a bare 'no funds' and no reserved balance (BalanceResponse has no reserved field; noneSelectableReason filters reserved UTXOs out before computing a reason), which also makes ChannelFunding._noCandidatesReason's held: predicate dead code for exactly the case it was added for.

title: Transaction lockTime and version are fabricated by the Isar and Postgres backends
description:
Found by the libspiffy-1kd5 reachability sweep; see doc/reachability-sweep-2026-09-18.md section 4, D-1.

BitcoinTransaction.lockTime and .version are carried correctly on the write path (TransactionImportedEvent.txLockTime / .txVersion, stored by wallet_projection) but NEITHER the Isar entity NOR the Postgres transactions table has a column for them. Both toDomain() paths therefore invent a value:

  libspiffy_schemas.dart:872   lockTime: 0,  // Would need to parse from rawHex or store separately
  libspiffy_schemas.dart:873   version: 1,
  postgres_wallet_storage.dart:1217  lockTime: 0, // Not stored in DB, default to 0
  postgres_wallet_storage.dart:1218  version: 1,

The in-memory backend stores the object and returns the real values, so the SAME wallet answers differently on different backends and the read-model contract tests do not cover it.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: a channel refund transaction is defined by its nLockTime. Read back as 0 it says "spendable now" about a transaction that is not. The reading is not absent, it is inverted.

rawHex IS stored, so the values are recoverable.

FIX: add the columns (Isar schema field + Postgres migration v023) and backfill by parsing rawHex where rawHex is present. Where there is no rawHex there is no evidence: follow the V-80 precedent (nullable blockHeight) and prefer int? over a plausible default, noting the breaking change to the public model.

TEST: a read-model contract test (test/storage/*_contract.dart, runs against all three backends) that stores a transaction with lockTime 500000123 and version 2 and reads it back. Must fail on Isar and Postgres today and pass on in-memory.
close_reason: Fixed on main as V-88 and V-89
